## Spider-Man: Brand New Day: Feeling on a Par with a Superhero

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/chelovek-pauk-novyy-den-2026/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-08-03 (3 August 2026)
Work: “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” is a 2026 film directed by Destin Daniel Cretton.
Tags: superheroes, blockbuster
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/chelovek-pauk-novyy-den-2026/

[*Spider-Man: Brand New Day*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1687) lets every viewer feel on a par with a superhero.

Doing so could not be easier, because in the new instalment Peter Parker appears as someone starting over from scratch, slightly burnt out and, like any young adult, confused. It seems the friendly neighbour could not have been any different in 2026: this new sincerity in Tom Holland’s portrayal is winning at the very least, and at most it reboots the franchise perfectly. Let me remind you that after the previous instalment, as a result of Doctor Strange’s spell, everyone in the world (even those closest to the hero) forgot Peter Parker.

The adventures of Spider-Man in a world where he loses not only his external but also his internal supports look more than plausible. The most varied special effects are, of course, in place and at their best, but Parker’s flights between skyscrapers look convincing not only thanks to the cool graphics. Holland has made his Spider-Man not just a “neighbour” but a true contemporary, who learns to find support within himself and to give it to others, even when it seems the critical point has come. But he does his superheroing: turning enemies into friends, emptiness into connections, and all of it to a cool soundtrack.

Maybe, in 2026, that is the main superpower.

## Monsters, Inc.: The Speech Quirks That Dubbing Hides

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/korporatsiya-monstrov-2001/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-07-28 (28 July 2026)
Work: “Monsters, Inc.” is a 2001 film directed by Pete Docter, David Silverman, Lee Unkrich.
Tags: animation, dubbing, rewatch
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/korporatsiya-monstrov-2001/

Healing my psyche after [this](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/den-razoblacheniya-2026/) took a rewatch of ~~Heated Rivalry~~ **Monsters, Inc.** in the original. [As usual](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/shrek-2001/), I tracked the quirks of speech that the dubbing hides from us:

- The most meme-worthy pet names of Wazowski and his beloved, which recently went viral as a trend, sound in Russian like “Zmeyusik-lapusik” and “Kruglik-bublik” (roughly “snakey-sweetie” and “roundy-bagel”). In English they are, respectively, Schmoopsie-poo and Googley Bear (sometimes Googley-woogley). This seems to be a case where the dubbing won)

- The little girl Boo was voiced by the three-year-old daughter of one of the voice actors, so in the original this little heroine sounds literally like a real child.

- And the next two points are for the most well-watched. Roz, the obnoxious administrator who torments Wazowski with bureaucratic nitpicking, when she reveals her true role, talks exactly like the fixer Mike Ehrmantraut from *Better Call Saul*/*Breaking Bad*. His famous “That's what happens next” matches the animated heroine right down to the intonation, and that is astonishing.

- The main villain, the purple lizard Randall, in one scene (comically enough, in the locker room) gives off the most brutal Rozanov vibes from *Heated Rivalry*. If you have watched the series, you will not be able to miss the similarity of intonation in the phrase “Aha, sure” with its villainously blunt mockery. The character was wonderfully voiced by Steve Buscemi)

## Disclosure Day: A Spielberg Thriller with a Fantastically Bad Script

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/den-razoblacheniya-2026/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-07-27 (27 July 2026)
Work: “Disclosure Day” is a 2026 film directed by Steven Spielberg.
Tags: science fiction, thriller
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/den-razoblacheniya-2026/

**Disclosure Day** turned my day off into a day of disappointment.

Steven Spielberg’s thriller with a fantastically bad script, and with Emily Blunt and Josh O’Connor, literally traumatised me.

In the first half of the film about two humans chosen by an alien intelligence who are trying to come to terms with their gift, there was nothing particularly suspicious. A few genre conventions, solemn faces, thoughts of saving the planet, if not the entire universe: standard stuff. The bend-over-backwards move of having Blunt’s heroine speak Russian with the appropriate accent is credited too, it actually perked me up ([I love that sort of thing](https://t.me/kino_voice/1213)).

But in the second half some kind of phantasmagorical absurdity began: a spectacle devoid of logic, credibility and common sense. The kindness of the plot or sweet nostalgia does not explain it. Specifically, the problems are these:

- It turns out that the characters began preparing for the appearance of the gifted Margaret (Blunt) even before they knew who would turn out to be the bearer of alien abilities at all. For the whole film they build a set that completely copies the heroine’s house and childhood bedroom, and then, with the most ingenuous look, are surprised to meet her.

- The collective antagonist that tormented the gifted pair for the whole film ultimately found its zen, so that the finale could unfold in “whatever will be, will be” mode, while the main villain sank into heavy thoughts about the fate of humanity.

- In the finale the heroes put classified footage of the aliens on air, and the broadcast is instantly picked up by channels in every state, and then around the world (there are shots of everyone in Russia glued to the screen). It is so true to life that in 2026 the world is still united by television. But do not worry, the authors have not forgotten about neural networks: one of the producers of one of the broadcasts in one of the states declared with an air of importance that the footage received was definitely not AI. You can literally see with the naked eye that the aliens in the footage are the real thing.

- The main characters, a fragile weather presenter and a lanky IT guy, managed to hold on for a considerable time to the bonnet of a mangled car being dragged along the rails at full speed by a train, and then also to jump onto a carriage while dodging an oncoming train. Not a single item of clothing torn, not a single wound, dislocation or bruise sustained: sleight of hand and no cheating. I understand that the film is science fiction, but any science fiction must be grounded in some rules of its screen world, not give the authors a free hand for complete nonsense.

- The alien device can do everything the script needs at any given moment and plugs any plot hole. The gadget lets you enter another person’s mind, take on anyone’s appearance and even generate electricity, in case the TV studio suddenly loses power (of course, the world has to learn the truth about the aliens from the television).

At best, while watching *Disclosure Day* I found it hysterically funny. But on reflection I have been indignant for three days now.

---

## Crowdfunding for the Short Film My edem khoronit dedushku

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/my-edem-khoronit-dedushku-kraudfanding/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-07-26 (26 July 2026)
Work: “My edem khoronit dedushku” is a work.
Tags: Russian cinema, short films, road movie, announcements
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/my-edem-khoronit-dedushku-kraudfanding/

Usually I write here about films that have already been made, but this time is an exception

A team of young filmmakers is shooting the short film [*My edem khoronit dedushku*](https://t.me/markandrus) («Мы едем хоронить дедушку», “We Are Going to Bury Grandpa”), a road movie about two brothers played by Makar Khlebnikov and Illarion Marov (actors I personally trust enormously).

From the description, a whole host of associations with great films springs to mind at once, from ***Kak Vitka Chesnok vyoz Lyokhu Shtyrya v dom invalidov*** («Как Витька Чеснок вез Леху Штыря в дом инвалидов», “How Vitka Chesnok Drove Lyokha Shtyr to the Home for the Disabled”) to [*She’s So Cool*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/ona-takaya-klassnaya-serial/) and [*Tantsuy, Seledka!*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/tantsuy-seledka-solntse-moe/) (“Dance, Seledka!”). In a word, a whole array of motifs that are important and interesting to watch in cinema, because this is our shared reality.

But for this film to happen, the team needs help: raising the rest of the money. The guys have opened a crowdfunding campaign where you can [make your contribution](https://planeta.ru/campaigns/markandru) and get in return tickets to the premiere, a thank-you in the credits and a lot of other nice things. This is exactly the case where the future of a promising project is in our hands as viewers, yours and mine, and this chance has to be taken.

Any good film is a huge chain of lucky breaks and coincidences, and I very, very much want *My edem khoronit dedushku* to be lucky.

## The Odyssey: The Quintessence of Nolan’s Directorial Signature

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/odisseya-2026/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-07-26 (26 July 2026); updated: 2026-07-30
Work: “The Odyssey” is a 2026 film directed by Christopher Nolan.
Tags: blockbuster, adaptation
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/odisseya-2026/

## 26 July 2026

**The Odyssey is my new favourite Christopher Nolan film.**

*Getting ahead of myself, I will headline this post with the thought that this seems to be the quintessence of Nolan’s directorial signature: all the Nolan themes (from the search for an unreachable home to responsibility for genius), the formal and structural devices with asynchronous narration and leaps in time, the actors’ appearances, are all here in peak form, the best possible. Surpassing the degree of perfection of each of these components of success is now within the power of, perhaps, only Nolan himself in his next work.*

First and foremost, this is a practically perfect screen adaptation of the familiar stories of ancient Greek folklore: the Cyclops, the Trojan horse, the giant Laestrygonians, Circe who turns sailors into pigs. Each of these stories is realised on screen so painstakingly and with such respect for its legendary status that for this reason alone I am ready to urge everyone to see this film. None of the stories with these creatures is some empty scare for the sake of a spike of adrenaline in the audience or an insert in the form of a spectacular attraction. They look, as befits elements of Homer’s *Odyssey*, monumental to the point of awe. I had never imagined a Cyclops looking like that, or the process of turning into pigs happening like that, because I could never have imagined these phenomena being so realistic, so inseparable from the elements of the world familiar to us. I simply fell in love with the way Nolan realised this and stitched it into the fabric of a spectacular blockbuster.

**\*️⃣** Incidentally, it is important to clarify that I took all the news about *The Odyssey* during filming and in the run-up to the premiere with a certain scepticism. Some of Nolan’s works (*Tenet*, for example) remained in my memory as a pretentious attempt to build a film on formal devices without particularly meaningful content, and the fear that the same would happen with *The Odyssey* was great. But all my sceptical thoughts were shattered by the magnificence of what I saw.

Do not be afraid of the three-hour running time (the pace of events ideally lets that time fly by unnoticed), of miscasting (there is none) or of the film’s convoluted structure: the balance of all the parts makes the picture truly outstanding and a must-see.

## 30 July 2026

What else makes [*The Odyssey*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1666) interesting is its gallery of characters and the key ideas they embody (and which lend themselves beautifully to memes).

 1️⃣Odysseus as played by Matt Damon is not shown as a trickster or a sly fox with a dash of comedy, as one might have expected looking back at the original text. Moreover, he is practically reduced to the “little man” who happens to live in a historic era (as if there were any reason to dwell on that subject in 2026), partly thanks to Damon’s type, since he has often had to play “ordinary guys”. The result is a hero utterly close to our perception, who, guided by the laws of his time (it happens to the best of us), made the decision to create the Trojan horse, and only later understood that there is something higher than the mores of an era. And the years the hero spent wandering in search of home, or simply in oblivion, can be interpreted in different ways, from PTSD to a liminal purgatory in which Odysseus pays for his moral crime. Even the memes about *The Odyssey* come with stills from *Oppenheimer*, where the hero himself regretted what he had invented.

**2️⃣** It is appropriate here to mention Athena as played by Zendaya: she acts as the materialisation of that timeless law of, if one may put it so, humanism, which Odysseus neglected. The shots of her silent condemnation have become memes about an extra ice cream eaten or hours spent scrolling the feed precisely because everyone knows disapproval of their own actions on various scales. So nothing human is alien to the hero of the ancient Greek poem, and that is one of the secrets of the film’s success.

**3️⃣** The memes about Penelope, the bow and the suitors feasting on Ithaca cover, if only superficially, the second most important plot vertical of *The Odyssey*. In my view, the film gives it slightly less attention than it could have, but the priorities are still set correctly. While someone is trying to return home, someone else gets to watch that home literally cease to exist and fill up with people who should not be there. Both funny, as the memes suggest, and sad beyond belief.

---

## Kidnapping: A Worthwhile Chameleon Thriller with an Outstanding Ensemble

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/pokhischenie-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-07-25 (25 July 2026)
Work: “Kidnapping” is a 2026 series directed by Kirill Pletnyov.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, thriller, mystery
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/pokhischenie-serial/

A [*Kidnapping*](https://youtu.be/yrEaOKm8w0Y?si=m8V-KrEa50xEURNR) has taken place: a very worthwhile chameleon thriller from Okko (the Russian streaming service) that is literally gripping to watch.

Judging by the first four episodes, it has almost everything: Timofey Tribuntsev as an investigator who addresses everyone as “kitten” (*kotik*, with the intonation from this [meme](https://t.me/kino_voice/1642)), Marina Vasilyeva, who is excellent as an absurdly contradictory heroine, and even Rinal Mukhametov, whose character has drug and mommy issues at the same time. This whole gallery of types has gathered over the disappearance in the woods of a five-year-old boy, and it is unclear whether there was a boy at all. But the company is outstanding, so even a plain human investigation against such a backdrop is rather interesting to follow.

* Andrey Zvyagintsev (Звягинцев Андрей Петрович) has been designated a “foreign agent” by Russia’s Ministry of Justice (listed on 18 September 2026).

## Pluribus and Heated Rivalry: The Parallel Release of Two Series as a Phenomenon

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/pluribus-heated-rivalry-paralleli/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-07-24 (24 July 2026)
Tags: series, analysis
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/pluribus-heated-rivalry-paralleli/

Naive parallels you did not need.

It seems that we as a society have not reflected enough on the fact that the parallel release of the series [*Pluribus*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/pluribus-serial/) and [*Heated Rivalry*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1205) is a phenomenon in itself.

**Pluribus** showed a universe where the heroine, a writer, had created a series of stunningly popular fantasy novels whose main characters were in a conventional relationship, while she herself considered her work mediocre and hypocritical, because she could not count on success for the unconventional romantic line she really wanted to describe. She had to go on writing, to please the fandom, about the kind of love that suited the readers.

In reality, in parallel with the release of this series, the whole world was also watching **Heated Rivalry**, the screen adaptation of precisely such a novel, in whose case the writer did not bet on traditional mores and wrote as she felt. Need I point out that a certain popularity (to put it mildly) is what both the series and the book got in the end?

*And what if Carol Sturka from Pluribus had written the novel she always wanted, without looking over her shoulder at public taste? Would that have worked, in the end, as a butterfly effect towards a turn into the branch of reality where no armageddon happens?* Think about it.

One way or another, it is good that the apocalypse happens in the universe where creativity is limited by prejudice. And for our reality, apparently, all is not yet lost.

---

## Restlessness: The Heroes Find Themselves in Something Like a Quantum Purgatory

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/nepokoy-2025/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-07-20 (20 July 2026); updated: 2026-08-07
Work: “Restlessness” is a 2025 film directed by Leonid Shmelkov.
Tags: animation, interview
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/nepokoy-2025/

## 20 July 2026

A great rarity: behind this stylish poster hides a no less intricately composed film, [*Restlessness*](https://youtu.be/3Qiu-KRJsMw?si=_BSi1e_hxAMYkxnI) (*Nepokoy*).

The plot of this adult animation is unpretentious precisely because quite early on it dissolves in favour of a controlled chaos of events, whose interpretation is left to the viewer’s discretion.

Yasha and Bernard are driving together to an unnamed distant destination and decide to spend the night on the way at an ordinary, moderately shabby roadside hotel called the Rosa. And there everything turns out to be stranger than strange.

Perhaps, without going into the details of what happens, it would be fair to say that the heroes have found themselves in something like a quantum purgatory. The hotel has a Madame, who is receptionist, cook, chambermaid and entertainer in one: she makes breakfasts from the dishes of roughly every cuisine in the world, hosts concerts, film clubs and all sorts of garden games. Only none of this gives the new guests any pleasure, because leaving the hotel proves impossible, first physically and then mentally.

What the hotel will be for you, and what the numerous metaphorical turns of the plot will turn into, is a matter of associations, imagination, viewing experience (if you wish, you will see Lynchian absurdity, and if you wish, a Wes Anderson aesthetic) and of the desire to reflect: *Restlessness* gives you full scope for that. For myself, I formulated what I saw as an extended visualisation of the opposite of what Pushkin wrote in the lines *“there is no happiness in the world, but there is peace and freedom”*. When there is everything for happiness but no possibility of making an independent decision in its favour, restlessness begins.

And this specific *Restlessness* can be experienced in cinemas (and only in cinemas; no release on streaming platforms has been announced) from 30 July.

## 7 August 2026

After [this interview](https://www.kinopoisk.ru/media/article/4013087/) I wanted to rewatch [*Restlessness*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1648).

Director Leonid Shmelkov talks about the concept of this feature-length animation in such a way that you literally discover some things anew. It was pleasant to find that I had defined the essence of the pink hares and the annoying runners who flash on screen more than once exactly as was intended.

---

## Cold: An Immersion That Knocks You Off Your Feet

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/kholod-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-07-16 (16 July 2026); updated: 2026-09-22
Work: “Cold” is a 2026 series directed by Aleksey Kazakov.
Tags: series, interview
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/kholod-serial/

## 16 July 2026

From today you can watch [*Cold*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1629) (*Kholod*), a chilling series with Lyubov Aksyonova.

When I watched the first episode, I literally lost track of time: from about the fifth minute I was simply clutching my head, trying not to start voicing the scale of the plot catastrophe out loud in unprintable language. The sheer number of misfortunes that befall Zhenya, Aksyonova’s heroine, at times really makes you forget to breathe. The very case where, while watching a series, you are not once tempted to check your phone.

At the same time Zhenya is so resilient, enduring and patient that it is hard to deny her sympathy, and the desire to root for her is the main motivation to watch to the end. Every scene shows very directly what kind of real deprivation is at stake (moral and physical), without sparing the viewer and without trying, as it were, to “hide” the uncomfortable moments of the story outside the frame. A series of rare sincerity about the powerlessness of the little man before the unjust blows of fate.

## 6 August 2026

In a recent interview with Sobchak (the Russian TV journalist), Lyubov Aksyonova told a story that is hard to forget: her father spent 4 years in a penal colony and then proved his innocence in court. She was 19. Now she plays Zhenya in [*Cold*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1643), a drama from Ivi, START and Wink (Russian streaming services) about a woman unjustly convicted over a car accident. When you know this, you look at the role quite differently.

Today my [interview](https://theblueprint.ru/culture/specials/cold-interview) with Lyubov Aksyonova, Linda Lapiņš and Alexandra Babaskina came out in The Blueprint. We talked about trauma, how it breaks you, makes you grow up and sometimes becomes a source of strength, and about how to stay human through all these trials.

Inside there is a lot that the trailer will not tell you: why Aksyonova, for the first time in her career, drew up a detailed map of her character and why the early Zhenya went by the code name “Snegurochka” (the Snow Maiden); Lapiņš’s real story of a girl whose fate seemed predetermined but which ended at Yale University; and why Sasha Babaskina is sure that children are sometimes stronger than adults.

The piece turned out insanely beautiful, not only in its ideas but visually: special love to the photographer Maxim Tarakanov and the whole team

As always, I picked out the quote that is key for me; it was voiced by Lyubov Aksyonova ⤵️

> *Cold* is a story about how, even from the most terrible ordeal, a person always has the chance to come out towards love and to lean on it. Love can turn out to be stronger than the desire to destroy. And only love can really defeat death. And that, probably, is the most important thing for me.

By the way, after the conversation with the actresses the following episodes look different: you begin to notice how Zhenya changes her body language, the rhythm of her speech and even her breathing from one period to the next. I checked it myself.

You can read the piece [at the link](https://theblueprint.ru/culture/specials/cold-interview).

## 15 September 2026

I deliberately saved up more episodes of [*Cold*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1643) to watch them in one go, and I was not wrong.

The series, and Lyubov Aksyonova’s performance in particular, has an immersive effect that somehow knocks you off your feet. I lost my sense of connection with reality during the first two episodes, and I lost it again watching all the following episodes back to back.

All thanks to what I would call “the aura of a thick novel”. This series is nothing like the typical alternation of events and consequences for various characters. *Cold* gives the impression of a vast canvas woven from a multitude of threads in different shades. First, the “threads” are never lost, even if they may meet again many years later. Second, among them there is anything you like except black and white. Third, while this “canvas” is being woven, it is worth stocking up on patience, just like the heroine, Zhenya. And the “embroidery” is so dense that you feel a physical urge to “reread” the series even before the finale. I am really looking forward to the last episode.

## 22 September 2026

Wrapping up the conversation about [*Cold*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1772)

I took part [in a poll by colleagues from Kinopoisk](https://www.kinopoisk.ru/media/article/4013398): we exchanged opinions on the series’ finale. I am pleased, which shows in my rating of 9/10 too, but what seems especially important to me is the gap left for the viewer’s hope in the closing frames. What matters is not even that Aksyonova’s heroine had some choice and some decision was made, but rather the reminder that after the most terrible ordeals a person retains some power over themselves, even if the outside world cannot be controlled. Lyubov [told me about this in our interview](https://t.me/kino_voice/1698), and it is great that exactly this is felt by the end of the viewing.

I separately recommend reading my colleagues’ opinions: each of us took a liking to (or, conversely, remembered with a negative context) something different. And I invite you to the comments; I am sure there is plenty to discuss ⬇️

---

## The Holy Boy: When the Village Would Be Better Off Without Its Righteous Man

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/dolina-ulybok-2025/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-07-13 (13 July 2026)
Work: “The Holy Boy” is a 2025 film directed by Paolo Strippoli.
Tags: horror, drama
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/dolina-ulybok-2025/

In cinemas now: [*The Holy Boy*](https://youtu.be/G7DFSS3WGH0?si=x8BHvR6czpg-vqMD) (*La valle dei sorrisi*, released in Russia as *Dolina ulybok*, “The Valley of Smiles”), an Italian horror drama about a strange town where everyone is far too happy.

The plot develops around Sergio, a PE teacher withdrawn after the loss of someone close (we are kept starved of specifics about the loss for a very long time), who comes to the town of Remis for 3 months as a substitute. At first glance he notices the suspiciously elevated mood all around, and then finds out for certain: the town has its own saint, who heals those suffering from grief after losing loved ones. The miraculous abilities belong to Matteo, a 15-year-old schoolboy, who gradually takes over the status of protagonist.

*The Holy Boy* seems to be the case where, contrary to the proverb (the Russian saying has it that no village stands without a righteous man), the village would be better off without its righteous man. And the problem is not Matteo himself but how the locals treat him: their consumerism is what serves as the trigger of the catastrophe. The script, incidentally, lets you focus your attention on the most varied aspects, from the difficulties of growing up and the problems of parenthood to a condemnation of the current trend for non-toxic communication, processed traumas and all the rest. At times, admittedly, so much is left unsaid that it starts to resemble plot holes, but that is a question of one’s personal readiness for small abstractions.

Incidentally, before the screening you should bear in mind that a couple of moments will be missing: these days not all of the film’s scenes meet the requirements for showing on the big screen, but it is good that on the whole it has made it to us.

In Venice, at any rate, *The Holy Boy* received the award of the Federation of Italian Film Clubs. So there is something to discuss there after watching.

---

## Fuss: So Far More Derivative Than Original

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/sueta-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-07-07 (7 July 2026)
Work: “Fuss” is a 2026 series directed by Anton Rodin.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, crime, comedy
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/sueta-serial/

I have watched [*Fuss*](https://youtu.be/fR0a8jRoUiM?si=0Ze_zk9VxyyAcXM8) (*Sueta*), but did not quite catch the spirit of the Pyatigorsk fussologists.

In the plot about four guys who decide to rob a cash-in-transit van but get into additional trouble, there is so far rather more that is derivative than original. The charm of petty southern crime loses out to projects like [*SWWW*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/yuzzz-serial/), and all the adventures of the hapless robbers seem to lack a false bottom: the bumbling heroes of [*Inkassatory*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/inkassatory-serial/) («Инкассаторы», “The Cash Collectors”), for instance, looked far more convincing breaking through the bottom of stupidity.

So far the cast is a joy: all the actors hit their types perfectly, and the role of a car-enthusiast robber suits Denis Vlasenko very well indeed. I hope a pleasant surprise awaits me in the next episodes.

## Nam kranty: A Convincing Trio of Hapless Friends and a Gallant Gangster

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/nam-kranty-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-07-06 (6 July 2026); updated: 2026-07-31
Work: “Nam kranty” is a 2026 series directed by Alexandr Sobichevsky.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, dramedy, crime
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/nam-kranty-serial/

## 6 July 2026

*Popados* (“Busted”) has turned into ***Nam kranty*** («Нам кранты», “We’re Toast”) and has moved closer to its premiere.

A really cool series that I [wrote about back at last year’s Pilot](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/festival-pilot-2025/) (the Russian series festival in Ivanovo): I had been waiting for it, and finally there is news. Three ordinary friends accidentally land in a criminal mess, and new problems start piling up in their lives. We will see all their adventures at a very dynamic pace, with mischievous jokes and, of course, action scenes.

The cast includes Makar Khlebnikov, Timofey Tribuntsev, Elizaveta Ishchenko and other actors who are a pleasure to follow. The premiere on Kion (the Russian streaming service) is, by all appearances, just around the corner.

## 31 July 2026

Today all the episodes of [*Nam kranty*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1626) came out on Kion: a moderately serious dramedy about why you should not flirt with the criminal world.

Judging by the first episodes, it is gripping to watch, even if not one hundred per cent new. But the devil is in the details, or rather, in the main characters. Makar Khlebnikov, Anton Shokalyuk and Sharifbek Zakirov make a very convincing trio of hapless friends whose types (the “schemer”, the “follower” and the “undecided one”) are familiar to everyone.

The older characters are not one bit worse. Over the season, the pensive security guard played by Timofey Tribuntsev is clearly going to come into his own. And the brazen grin of crime is the job of the gallant gangster played by Andrey Prytkov. His temperament, by the standards of central Russia, is practically Mexican.

---

## Diary of a Wimpy Kid: A Funny, Dynamic Film for Viewers of All Ages

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/dnevnik-slabaka-2010/
Author: Betsy Isakova

Work: “Diary of a Wimpy Kid” is a 2010 film directed by Thor Freudenthal.
Tags: comedy, family, adaptation, American cinema
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/dnevnik-slabaka-2010/

*Found the meme about badly singing kids in its natural habitat*

My experience of watching ***Diary of a Wimpy Kid***, by the way, was marked by more than just that. The picture is generally rich in memes: for instance, it has the absolutely canonical image of the wild older brother, who has been cut up into countless viral clips. They started popping up obsessively in my feed and in the end nudged me into watching. Alas, almost all the funny moments with him are in the second part, so I got caught out twice.

Nevertheless, it would not be amiss to say that I was very surprised by the crossover of these universes. And even if you set aside the delight of meeting a meme in the wild, the first part is very funny and dynamic for viewers of all ages (which is rather a rarity). At some moments I even caught niche overlaps between one of the characters and Vovan from *Real Boys* («Реальные пацаны», the long-running Russian TV sitcom set in Perm); please don’t be jealous, it is purely a matter of how much you have watched.

And I will definitely watch the second part of *Diary of a Wimpy Kid*, and this time with certain expectations.

## Raz malchishka, dva malchishka: Short in Length, but a Very Palpable Read

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/raz-malchishka-dva-malchishka-kniga/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-07-04 (4 July 2026)
Work: “Raz malchishka, dva malchishka” is a 2024 book by Asya Demishkevich.
Tags: books, horror
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/raz-malchishka-dva-malchishka-kniga/

I do not very often like anything from contemporary literary fiction in Russian, but recently, on a recommendation, I read Asya Demishkevich’s novel [*Raz malchishka, dva malchishka*](https://books.yandex.ru/books/iVnOelfS?utm_campaign=users_referral&amp;utm_medium=referral&amp;utm_source=direct_link) («Раз мальчишка, два мальчишка», “One Boy, Two Boys”) practically in one breath, and now I am going to recommend it to you.

I do not know how to characterise its genre more precisely: it is a coming-of-age novel, folk horror and topical allegorical absurdity all at once. Thirteen-year-old Andrey is sent off to the army by his wicked stepmother (the morphology of the fairy tale crops up often in this text, do not be surprised), and there everything is somehow strange: the squad includes a couple of dead men, there are no barracks at all, and in their place iron bedsteads stand in a bare field under the open sky.

The further adventures of the “recruits” are more interesting to read than to learn from a retelling, so here I will limit myself to general raptures. Demishkevich’s style is contemporary in the best sense of the word, and this shows not in attempts to mimic the plausible speech of a Russian teenager! I am talking about the complete removal of the boundaries between the reader and what is happening, which are usually, conventionally, represented precisely by the author’s style. The words seem to narrate and comment on the events for the reader all by themselves (and there is plenty in those events to think about and to laugh at). And the ending, in my view, for all its unexpectedness, is more than logical. Short in length, but very palpable in its impressions.

---

~~Ilia Malinin, Snoop Dogg,~~ [*Get Back On Your Feet*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/vstat-na-nogi-serial/), [*Radar*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1519), [*Pride*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1519): they are all here. In this piece, I personally wrote the entry on [*Posle Fishera. Inkvizitor*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/posle-fishera-serial/) («После Фишера. Инквизитор», “After Fisher. ## You Don’t Mess with the Zohan: One of the Best Sessions of Restorative Escapism

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/ne-shutite-s-zokhanom-2008/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-06-27 (27 June 2026)
Work: “You Don’t Mess with the Zohan” is a 2008 film directed by Dennis Dugan.
Tags: comedy
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/ne-shutite-s-zokhanom-2008/

I would never have thought that one of the best sessions of restorative escapism for me would be watching **You Don’t Mess with the Zohan**.

The plot about a counter-terrorist (Adam Sandler) who has grown tired of fighting and faked his own death to start a new life may seem one-layered. Perhaps its strength lies precisely in laying out all the between-the-lines meanings in plain view, so that each viewer picks the main ones according to their own inclination. And yes, the hummus jokes won me over. Yes, I watched it in the original, so I fell for the accents too ([apologise](https://t.me/kino_voice/1213)). Yes, the humour in the film is on the dark side and belongs rather to the “borderline good taste” category (if you have seen *Borat*, it is comparable). All this is paid off by one gigantic “but”, which those who have seen it will probably name easily, and those who have not (I envy you now) will surely be able to note while watching.

For all its frivolity, this is a film-cum-social utopia about what one would so like to see in the world but which is so impossible to achieve. Everyone does what they love. Disagreements are in the past. The sharpest remarks addressed to one’s neighbour are labelled in advance as jokes (and invite mutual ribbing). I do not know how this film passed me by in its day, but it found me, perhaps, at the best moment, and I hope it will brighten one of your evenings.

---

## Baranyi bega: Guy Ritchie Charm and an Off-the-Charts Number of Jokes

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/barani-bega-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-06-20 (20 June 2026)
Work: “Baranyi bega” is a 2026 series directed by Rashid Yusupov.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, comedy
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/barani-bega-serial/

***Baranyi bega*** («Бараньи бега», “The Ram Races”) has some off-the-charts number of genuinely funny jokes per square centimetre, both in the script and in the visuals, and even in the editing.

It is a story with a thoroughly Guy Ritchie-style charm. Two meat deliverymen in Dagestan are driving (apparently stolen) mutton to a hotel opening, but get a little carried away watching wrestling, so the journey drags on. A bag of money falls on them from a plane carrying some Russian gangsters from Georgia. True, the butcher brothers do not even get the chance to find out about it. At the very first stop the bag (together with the mutton) is stolen from the back of the truck by the hapless prop mistress of a local film crew (and film people, as the deliverymen put it, are more dangerous than Gypsies).

In short, everything whirls along at a very brisk pace, and the audience practically never stopped laughing from one joke to the next. I will be waiting for it on the streaming services.

---

## Problem Child: Tangible Madness and an Absolute Must-Watch Series

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/trudnyy-rebenok-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-06-20 (20 June 2026); updated: 2026-10-08
Work: “Problem Child” is a 2026 series directed by Vladimir Bolgov, Velimir Rusakov, Nikita Zubkov.
Tags: series, comedy
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/trudnyy-rebenok-serial/

## 20 June 2026

***Problem Child*** (*Trudny rebyonok*) is either an experimental absurdity or an absurd experiment. But it makes for a magnificent watch.

Professional footballer Filipp (Gennady Blinov) accidentally breaks his leg and finds himself forced to raise money for an operation, so he takes odd jobs, alternating between petty crime and history tutoring. And in the process everything gets so insane that the comedy rises to the level of some kind of total meta-humour, which is very enticing. Plus Mujuice on the soundtrack. I really want to see the rest: I was in stitches.

## 25 September 2026

I am watching [*Problem Child*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1764) with a kind of half-forgotten zest

The series has such a perceptible, tangible air of madness and inadequacy that it plunges you into an unnatural viewer’s comfort. Perhaps it would even be appropriate to call it “ecstasy”: wow, someone on screen has it even more unhinged than in real life. But even in such an upside-down, strange world there is room for love (all ages and social strata really are subject to it), friendship and optimism. And now the story of an injured footballer who moonlights as a tutor to pay for an operation and return to the sport plays in new colours.

 And all the actors are exactly in their places: I will now definitely be following the projects of Gennady Blinov (the footballer-historian) and Boris Deikov (the problem child himself).

A wonderful piece of work, and one with individuality against the background of many comedy series.

## 8 October 2026

I have finished [*Problem Child*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1788), and now I can say with confidence that it is an absolute must-watch series.

Besides what has already been praised in the posts above, something else needs noting. This is a rare case of a series whose pace does not sag or break in the middle of the season (a rarity these days): there is no urge to drop it or skip ahead to the end. Form here is in complete harmony with content, absurdity in both, but very well balanced. A separate bow to the screenwriters for the genuine urge to keep a notebook of quotes while watching.

And the footballer-historian joins my personal collection of characters in the category “you don’t want to be with him, you want to be him”. Stay tuned.

---

## Vor v zagone: A Sweet Comedy, and Kudos for Popularising Psychology

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/vor-v-zagone-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-06-20 (20 June 2026)
Work: “Vor v zagone” is a 2026 series directed by Artyom Lempert.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, comedy
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/vor-v-zagone-serial/

***Vor v zagone*** («Вор в загоне», “Thief in the Pen”, a pun on *vor v zakone*, “thief in law”) is that very project from Russian Code with Denis Vlasenko that I [had pinned my hopes on](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/pilot-2026-nezavisimye-proekty/).

Psychologist Anton (Denis Vlasenko) travels with his girlfriend Polina to Ust-Baikalsk to meet her parents. Things do not go to plan, and the head of the family (Vladimir Vdovichenkov) takes offence at Anton. The young man goes to the garage to build bridges with him and finds out that the man is holding someone hostage. The head of the family decides to test him and takes him along to torture the hostage, but the hostage escapes because of Anton. In the process Vdovichenkov’s character has a panic attack, and Anton helps him pull himself together, but he still rejects the young man. It turns out that Polina is pregnant, so Anton and the father of the family have to set their differences aside.

It is a sweet comedy, every actor is perfectly cast, and most importantly, kudos for popularising psychology and drawing attention to mental health. I will be looking forward to it.

---

## Alyosha Bozhiy chelovek: A Realistic Conversation with Viewers as Equals

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/alyosha-bozhiy-chelovek-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-06-19 (19 June 2026)
Work: “Alyosha Bozhiy chelovek” is a 2026 series directed by Mikhail Chistov.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, drama
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/alyosha-bozhiy-chelovek-serial/

Okko (the Russian streaming service) has started an interesting conversation about important subjects in cinema with the project ***Alyosha Bozhiy chelovek*** («Алёша Божий человек», “Alyosha, Man of God”; out of competition).

Its creators call the project a “cousin” of [*Second Wind*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/vtoroe-dykhanie-serial/). The pilot episode revolves around an ordinary grandmother who was almost killed by her own young grandson. She seriously considers that the grandson has been possessed by demons and tries to convince her daughter that the boy must be taken to a monastery, but in the end takes matters into her own hands.

This is not some tedious moralising canvas and not a comedy, but a very realistic conversation with viewers as equals. The camera looks into the kitchens of those grandmothers who have their kulich (Easter cake) blessed every Easter, and of those young parents who, because of their circumstances, have developed a certain indifference towards bringing up their children. As Gavriil Gordeev says, the series lets us witness the everyday condemnation of all of them that we ourselves feel but do not notice in daily life. We all know these people, and such precision on screen is astonishing; I hope we will soon be able to see the continuation.

---

## Klyatva Gippokrata: The Ambulance Service as a String of Funny Incidents

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/klyatva-gippokrata-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-06-19 (19 June 2026)
Work: “Klyatva Gippokrata” is a 2026 series directed by Nikita Andrienko.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, comedy
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/klyatva-gippokrata-serial/

And this close-knit team in merch was presenting the series ***Klyatva Gippokrata*** («Клятва Гиппократа», “The Hippocratic Oath”)

The young, overconfident surgeon Viktor Zhivykh (Konstantin Beloshapka) is sent by the chief physician (Pavel Derevyanko) to work on an ambulance as a punishment. His new colleagues, the paramedic Lyonya (Egor Ovchinnikov) and the driver Nikolaich (Andrey Fedortsov), amiably immerse their colleague in a new world (and at the same time help to re-educate the insolent Zhivykh).

The ambulance work in this series is more a string of funny incidents than the hard work of saving lives. But those are the conventions of the genre, and within its own concept the project is very pleasant: I will watch it to the end.

## Sokrovishcha skifov: A Solid Adventure Drama with Meme-Worthy Moments

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/sokrovischa-skifov-serial/

Published: 2026-06-19 (19 June 2026)
Work: “Sokrovishcha skifov” is a 2026 series directed by Evgeniy Bedarev.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, adventure
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/sokrovischa-skifov-serial/

***Sokrovishcha skifov*** («Сокровища скифов», “Treasures of the Scythians”) is a solid adventure drama inspired, according to its creators, by *Indiana Jones*.

As a TV series, it is a fairly interesting project. Linda Lapiņš plays Katya, a principled archaeologist, and a struggle for an ancient golden artefact unfolds around her and her son, who has taken an interest in archaeology. But the most unusual thing is some utterly meme-worthy moments that do not look deliberately tied to the story. A bodyguard with John Travolta’s face, gold hidden among the pelmeni (Russian dumplings) in the freezer, a packet of crisps that wanders into the bin and back. In short, it seems I will watch the next episodes)

## Affekt: A Minimalist Thriller That Deserves a Chance from Genre Fans

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/affekt-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-06-18 (18 June 2026)
Work: “Affekt” is a 2026 series directed by Vladislav Andreev.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, thriller
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/affekt-serial/

Judging by its first episode, the series *Affekt* («Аффект», “Affect”) plays as a minimalist high-concept psychological thriller.

Kirill, an ordinary taxi driver, becomes the unwitting cause of a scooter rider’s death. He falls into a state of affect (a fit of passion, in the legal sense) and, whether in his head or in reality, meets a talkative investigator who tells him a story of an accidental killing that is an exact match, along with a way to cover up the deed. Having said goodbye to his passenger, the driver rushes to put what he has heard into practice at once, and so begins his connection with crime.

Among its undeniable merits is a consistent visual resemblance to the film *Centaur* («Кентавр»). Otherwise, there are pluses and minuses, but it certainly deserves a chance from fans of the genre.

---

## Jive: An Heir to On the Ice About the Brutal Side of Spectator Sport

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/dzhayv-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-06-18 (18 June 2026)
Work: “Jive” is a 2026 series directed by Danil Chashchin.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, sport, drama
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/dzhayv-serial/

***Jive*** is in many ways an heir to *On the Ice*, another high-octane project from Okko (the Russian streaming service) about the brutal side of spectator sport.

In Moscow, a fierce rivalry unfolds between the strongest couples of ballroom dancers. Each of them has their own context, their own dream and their own (let’s be honest) nervous breakdown, but not everyone knows that their own coach may be swaying the judging in favour of other people’s dancers for money. Meanwhile, David Sokratyan’s hero runs away from a remote village, literally on an ancient motorcycle with a sidecar. It is he who sets off a chain of changes in the tight-knit dancers’ ~~community~~ snake pit.

I will keep watching; I am curious to see where it goes from here.

---

## Second Wind: A Story That Gets Under Your Skin

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/vtoroe-dykhanie-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-06-18 (18 June 2026)
Work: “Second Wind” is a 2026 series directed by Ruslan Bratov.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, drama
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/vtoroe-dykhanie-serial/

The pilot episode of ***Second Wind*** from Okko (the Russian streaming service) makes an incredible impression ([just as I had supposed](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/pilot-2026-nezavisimye-proekty/)).

They are trying to commit Ilya (Alexander Pal) to a motivational centre to cure him of his addiction. From the very doorstep it turns out to be an absurd, cruel world with rules beyond the limits of human empathy. A name alone is not enough to introduce yourself, because it must be followed by the term “alcoholic” or “drug addict”, depending on the dependency. Ilya refuses to admit to any such thing, sets himself against the whole local order and begins to plot an escape.

The project is very strong, and not only in its meaning and chosen theme. The visual touches (for example, the numerous references to *Fight Club*) and the 4:3 frame format, “cramped” just like the hero’s constrained circumstances, convince you on a subconscious level. And so the whole story seems to get under your skin, leaving you no chance to tear yourself away. Watching to the end is a must.

---

## Living Anew: The Series That Came Out Suspiciously Quietly

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/zhizn-zanovo-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-06-18 (18 June 2026); updated: 2026-11-04
Work: “Living Anew” is a 2026 series directed by Aleksandr Boguslavskiy.
Tags: series, streaming
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/zhizn-zanovo-serial/

## 18 June 2026

**Living Anew** (*Zhizn zanovo*), which was among the things I was [looking forward to](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/pilot-2026-nezavisimye-proekty/) with interest, has fully lived up to expectations.

The time-travel comedy looks like a very gripping, solid piece of work. Alexander Yatsenko, in the role of an ambulance doctor tired of life and of his own inadequacy, is very convincing, as *Arrhythmia* showed, and this series uses that advantage 100%. The humour here is charming and unhackneyed, so watching is a great pleasure.

As a result of an MRI machine breaking down, the hero from our time is transported to 2002, and the panorama of St Petersburg in the 2000s, shown to the music of Glukoza (the Russian pop singer), simply takes your breath away. The cinema is showing *Progulka* (“The Stroll”), and every student has a pager on their belt. And the hero himself finds himself in that time with all the knowledge of his 40 years, which he puts to use in his own way.

A super project, which I will await impatiently and will definitely watch to the end.

## 4 November 2026

The series [*Living Anew*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1558) came out on the streaming platforms suspiciously quietly, and I, as I had planned since Pilot (the Russian series festival), am continuing to watch it.

Everything is done attractively, rhythmically (perfect for watching many episodes in a row!) and without the dreary clichés inherent in the time-travel genre. Not without some confusion in its moral compass, but Dima the doctor (Alexander Yatsenko/Anton Shavrin) in 2002 tirelessly extricates himself from one mishap after another, trying meanwhile not to incur the notorious butterfly effect, and he does it rather wittily. A compliment to the script and the costume designers: the wardrobe of Lenya, the protagonist’s best friend, is so stylish that you want to steal the whole lot for personal use in 2026.

The main advantage, which reveals itself after a few episodes, is the perfect casting of the characters in their youth and in adulthood. Anton Shavrin (the young version of Yatsenko) wonderfully conveys the state of a forty-year-old doctor locked in the body of an 18-year-old student, a real find of the series. Robert Zakharyan, who plays Artyom Tkachenko’s character from 2002, is altogether a most successful comic type; I hope he will reveal himself further in that capacity. And I very much like the heroines in their youth: Alisa and Kristina are played by Elizaveta Ishchenko and Margarita Dyachenkova (whom I have been following for a long time, because we have known each other since school), and each has an elusive intonation carried over from her adult version (Karina Razumovskaya and Elena Podkaminskaya respectively).

I have a few final episodes left for dessert, and I am stretching them out as best I can.

---

## ZhPT: A Neural Network Can Do a Lot, but Creative Embodiment Is a Human Privilege

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/zhpt-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-06-18 (18 June 2026)
Work: “ZhPT” is a 2026 series directed by Yana Rubanovskaya.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, documentary
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/zhpt-serial/

The curious project ***ZhPT*** («ЖПТ», a play on “GPT” in Russian letters) is devoted to unconventional ways of using neural networks.

The host, Karen Adamyan, travels around Russian cities and explores how local businesses, producers and ordinary people can be helped by building artificial intelligence into their work. It is shot in the best traditions of travel shows, and on top of that it improves digital literacy, popularises neural networks and boosts their reputation. In the first episode, a luge coach, a restaurant owner and an architect from Kandalaksha got acquainted with AI. And Karen himself dived into icy water, having enlisted the support of a neural-network psychologist in his earpiece.

I hope the project finds its target audience — the mix of themes is unconventional. The main thing is that the central idea is very harmonious: a neural network can come up with or optimise a lot, but creative embodiment and realisation are always a human right and privilege.

---

## Pilot 2026: Independent Projects I Want to See in Full

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/pilot-2026-nezavisimye-proekty/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-06-17 (17 June 2026); updated: 2026-06-22
Tags: festivals, series, Russian cinema
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/pilot-2026-nezavisimye-proekty/

## 17 June 2026

I am diving into the film festival atmosphere: [Pilot](https://t.me/kino_voice/1514) (the Russian series festival in Ivanovo) is starting, which means that over the next 5 days this channel will fill up with reviews of the first episodes of all kinds of series.

I skimmed the (very extensive) programme in advance and noted down the projects whose descriptions sound most interesting.

- ***Vor v zagone*** («Вор в загоне», “A Thief in the Pen”, a play on *vor v zakone*, “thief in law”): a series with Denis Vlasenko (you remember my [principles](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/pro-eto-samoe-serial/)). A comedy about a psychologist who studies his fiancée’s relatives and assigns each of them a mental disorder of their own. I hope it turns out to be *About This Very Thing* with a psychological slant

- ***Festival*** («Фестиваль»): a series about a film festival, and what could be better than watching something like that at a film festival?! The director is Alexey Kamynin, who previously made the wonderful and very funny film *Khandra* («Хандра», “The Blues”). The cast of the new project includes Daniil Vorobyov, Mikhail Troynik and, by the way, my colleague [Artyom Remizov](https://t.me/remizorro)

- ***Second Wind***: a tragicomedy by Ruslan Bratov with Alexander Pal, about searching for yourself in life and difficult relationships with loved ones. I believe Bratov will tell this story in a dramatically funny way.

- ***Jive***: a high-octane project about dancesport from the production company Sreda for Okko (the Russian streaming service), so I expect the quality to match. Starring David Sokratyan, Anastasia Ukolova, Svyatoslav Rogozhan and lots of cool young actors.

- ***Living Anew***: a comedy about a second chance to live your best years (in the literal and figurative sense: the main character is transported from the present day to 2002). Starring Alexander Yatsenko, Elena Podkaminskaya and other actors who are always believable. Shades of [*Comeback*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/kambek-serial/), judging by the era.

- ***Pasha*** with Askar Ilyasov ([I wrote about it here](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/pasha-serial/))

## 18 June 2026

The block of independent projects at Pilot (the Russian series festival in Ivanovo) is over, and here are the projects I hope we will see in full in the future:

**GBU “Zhizn”** («ГБУ „Жизнь“», “State Institution ‘Life’”)

As the project’s team put it, “we tell the story of traditional values in a non-traditional way”. The series will be devoted to an unusual funeral home that tries to make even the part of life connected with death life-affirming. A soft, blackish (naturally) but very likeable comedy.

***Volshebnaya pyl*** («Волшебная пыль», “Magic Dust”)

A talented chemist (Yulia Volkova) loses her job and suddenly discovers that her neighbour is cooking up something suspicious. Having wrecked the neighbour’s home-cosmetics business with her vigilance, the woman is plotting something.

***Vverkh za mechtoy*** («Вверх за мечтой», “Up After the Dream”)

A romantic comedy with Polina Denisova and Grisha Vernik. An underrated producer is forced to work with an arrogant showman (and former classmate at that), but their enmity gradually gives way to passion. The “from hatred to love” mechanism works brilliantly in cinema, and I have known one of the producers, Liza Bulatova, since school, so I believe in this story.

***Privet, Karolinka*** («Привет, Каролинка», “Hi, Karolinka”)

A children’s adventure fantasy about a girl who investigates the mysterious disappearance of her grandmother with the help of a magic piece of chalk. The project’s highlight is that the main villain is played by the stylist Alexander Rogov. The spiritual heir of *Lyubopytnaya Varvara* (“Curious Varvara”, the children’s detective series), which means a bid for a quality children’s series.

## 19 June 2026

The morning begins with independent projects: today it is science fiction, aliens and mockumentary.

*Shisha*

A project about a regional evil spirit who lives in the age of social networks and decides to relaunch its villainous brand to avoid the closure of the “Agency of Dirty Tricks”. For this, “Kolkhoz Production” is brought in. A little raw (which is absolutely normal for the pilot of an independent project), but already a very charming spiritual heir of *What We Do in the Shadows* and *The Magic District* (*Volshebny uchastok*).

*Kosmos nash* (“Space Is Ours”)

A blogger who films so-called contactees (people who have made contact with aliens) reaches a million subscribers and suddenly loses his dog. Instead he acquires a suspicious female fan with the manners of an alien. Also a pilot that is likeable at the level of its concept and has every chance of success after some polishing.

## 19 June 2026

Two decent television projects: ***Angel*** («Ангел») from TV-3 and ***Ilya Murovets*** («Илья Муровец», a play on the epic hero Ilya Muromets and MUR, the Moscow criminal investigation department) from Channel 5 (both are Russian TV channels).

In *Angel*, Kuzma Saprykin plays the angel Serafim, sent down from heaven to look after a female investigator who has recently lost her husband. A nod of sorts to the film *Moy paren angel* («Мой парень ангел», “My Boyfriend Is an Angel”). It stays in the memory for the perfect choice of actor for the angel, and also for comic moments on the edge between cringe and wisdom (I wrote down a quote for myself, for example: “if someone once wiped their feet on you, there is no point curling back up like a worn doormat”; the audience applauded).

*Ilya Murovets* is a police procedural with a fairy-tale accent. Everything is just as the Channel 5 representatives described it at the morning business programme: fairy-tale qualities according to Propp, magical helpers and a happy ending. The only letdown is the not-so-high-quality AI-generated inserts of the hero’s flashbacks from the past.

## 20 June 2026

Today’s block of independent projects pleased with youth themes:

***Kod 102*** («Код 102», “Code 102”)

Possibly the strongest independent project of this year. A vibey neon series about young musicians from Ufa who are trying to break through and realise their dream. The project has distinctive features: the colour of Bashkortostan and Ufa, the participation of local performers, and an excellent cast: Chingiz Garaev, Arseny Kasperovich, Pyotr Skvortsov and other cool artists.

***#Ne\_moya\_zhizn*** («#Не\_моя\_жизнь», “#Not_My_Life”)

A story about the destructive influence of social networks on our lives, told through teenage characters. A high-school girl who dreams of becoming a blogger accidentally finds a phone and starts posting videos from it. After that everything goes uphill for her, but as soon as the owner demands the phone back, the situation stops being pleasant.

***Tozhe mne lyubov*** («Тоже мне любовь», “Call That Love”)

A drama about different types of relationships: between romantic partners, between sisters, with oneself. All the relationships, naturally, are unhealthy. It looks very much in the spirit of the recent [*Half Man*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/half-man-serial/).

## 21 June 2026

And two more projects that seemed promising:

***The Captain’s Daughter*** («Капитанская дочка»): a fresh screen adaptation of the classic with Oleg Savostyuk, Evgeny Tkachuk, Viktoria Isakova and other distinguished actors. It sounds interesting and looks spectacular; it remains to be seen what the approach will be.

***Kamenskaya. Perezagruzka*** («Каменская. Перезагрузка», “Kamenskaya. Reboot”): a relaunch of the classic series (the 2000s detective show based on Alexandra Marinina’s novels) with Yulia Khlynina in the lead role. She played the investigator superbly in [*Overheard in Rybinsk*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/podslushano-v-rybinske-serial/), so I believe in this character too.

## 21 June 2026

All the winners of Pilot 2026

- Best series pilot: [*Second Wind*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/vtoroe-dykhanie-serial/)
- Best series pilot (audience choice): [*Problem Child*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/trudnyy-rebenok-serial/)
- Best director of a series pilot: Ruslan Bratov ([*Second Wind*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/vtoroe-dykhanie-serial/))
- Best pilot screenplay: Anton Kolomeets and Evgeniya Tamakhina ([*Pasha*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/pasha-serial/))
- Best ensemble cast: the series [*Festival*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1597) («Фестиваль»)
- Best actor in a series: Askar Ilyasov ([*Pasha*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/pasha-serial/))
- Best actress in a series: Yulianna Mikhnevich (who appeared in three series at the festival)
- Best documentary series: [*Virus popsy*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1556) («Вирус попсы», “The Pop Virus”)
- Best second season of a series: [*Old School*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1574)
- Most anticipated series: *Krasnaya shambala* («Красная шамбала», “Red Shambhala”)

## 22 June 2026

Pilot 2026 is over, and [Olya](https://t.me/hightechlowlifee) and I have gathered all the festival’s series for Kinopoisk (Russia’s largest film database, media and streaming service) [in a single selection](https://www.kinopoisk.ru/media/article/4012907/).

The programme this year is (to my taste) strong, and I talked about my most vivid impressions here during the festival. And from the piece, be sure to pay attention to the award-winning series: they are an absolute must-watch on every count (Askar Ilyasov personally advised me to watch *Pasha*, which starts on 10 July, all the way to the end, so there is every reason to take his word for it).

## 22 June 2026

And I simply cannot help sharing: I came back from Pilot charged for a whole year ahead with love for cinema, joy and the energy to share my favourite series and support their premieres.

The strongest programme, the most caring organisation and a practically family atmosphere: every year I am amazed at how good it is, and about an hour after the closing I start waiting for next year. It seems to me this is unique and priceless.

I value beyond measure the opportunity to be part of such a buzz, the trust of the organisers and your patience, dear readers (let’s be honest, such a flood of posts does not happen often). Thank you.

## Eto bylo v Rossii: A Patchwork Quilt of Musical and Media Culture

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/eto-bylo-v-rossii-kniga/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-06-15 (15 June 2026)
Work: “Eto bylo v Rossii: muzyka 2010-kh ot kalyan-repa do postpanka” is a 2025 book by Arkady Romanov.
Tags: books, music
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/eto-bylo-v-rossii-kniga/

And here is something else bookish: I have managed to get through practically all (apologies to the chapter on chanson, which I skipped) of the non-fiction book [*Eto bylo v Rossii*](https://books.yandex.ru/books/yRjtQWuE) («Это было в России», “It Happened in Russia”).

An extremely engrossing text, packed with facts, yet weightless. Many of the songs mentioned are familiar to us from Russian series (the book devotes almost a whole chapter to the electronic musician Mujuice, a regular of *Mir! Druzhba! Zhvachka!*, “Peace! Friendship! Bubblegum!”, the 1990s-set series)

Arkady Romanov combines Russia’s recent history with the biographies of the leading performers of the Russian scene and with social phenomena that we all witnessed but have not reflected on enough. This is how a patchwork quilt of musical and media culture is woven, one that is extremely interesting to relive, even from a short distance.

---

## Pasha: A Handcrafted Island of Calm in a World of Adrenaline Content

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/pasha-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-06-15 (15 June 2026); updated: 2026-08-04
Work: “Pasha” is a 2026 series directed by Anton Kolomeets, Evgeniya Tamakhina.
Tags: series, dramedy, Russian cinema
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/pasha-serial/

## 15 June 2026

A charming trailer for [*Pasha*](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MU5Z6wX_oVQ), the upcoming series from Amediateka (a Russian streaming service)

The dramedy with Askar Ilyasov will tell the story of a modest piano tuner, Pasha Belov: he was born in Moscow and studied at the Gnesinka (Moscow’s renowned Gnessin music school), but never became a musician, and he cannot find out anything about his Uzbek roots. I am glad that the series touches on a subject rarely talked about in Russian films and series: what it is like to be “one of us” and at the same time constantly run into being read as an outsider. Genre-wise, by all appearances, it will be a coming-of-age story, a conversation about identity and a sketch from the life of a Muscovite all at once. Irina Gorbacheva and Tatyana Dogileva also star, so the cast should be a treat.

I will write a review of the first episode from the [Pilot](https://t.me/kino_voice/1514) festival (the Russian series festival in Ivanovo) very soon, and the series premieres on 10 July.

## 20 June 2026

Once again a team in merch (I want some!!): Amediateka (a Russian streaming service) presents the series **Pasha** from my [list](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/pilot-2026-nezavisimye-proekty/) of things to look forward to.

Judging by the first episode, this is a very touching, sparkling dramedy with gentle humour and intonation. Pasha, a Muscovite who is half Uzbek by ethnicity (and therefore runs into every stereotype), is trying to find somewhere to live for 10 days, because his mother’s friend has settled into his own flat with a child who has chickenpox (and Pasha, as luck would have it, never had it). So the hero literally and figuratively cannot find a home in his native city.

As the creators said, Askar Ilyasov is present in every scene of the series. And I will add that he sets the tone and mood of everything that happens, and that creates something inimitable. The premiere is on 10 July, and I cannot wait.

## 14 July 2026

I carried on watching [*Pasha*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1590) after the first episode at Pilot (the Russian series festival in Ivanovo), and got exactly what I expected.

The series has an intonation rare these days, that of a kind of lyrical comedy where nothing especially funny seems to happen, sometimes even the opposite, something sad, and yet every so often you smile. Simply because life goes on, the sun peeks through the clouds, the neighbours act up and the relatives are toxic. Life does not end there, after all.

I will also keep watching closely because Askar Ilyasov promised something special in the seventh episode. Given that every episode of *Pasha* looks like a handcrafted island of calm in a world of adrenaline content, I am inclined to trust that advice.

## 4 August 2026

I watched all the episodes of [*Pasha*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1641) in one go and had the loveliest evening.

Askar Ilyasov promised that something special awaited us in episode 7, and he did not deceive us: it is the peak of the season in conviction, sincerity and the absence of any sense of a boundary between the two sides of the screen. But personally I was most moved by episode 6, whether it was the images of a Moscow school in the 2000s that touched a nerve, or the rare chance that materialised before little Pasha to replay a dysfunctional scenario, this time with a happy outcome (in the best traditions of contemporary psychology).

In any case, I highly recommend watching *Pasha*: the value lies not only in the image of the protagonist but in the scattering of types surrounding him. Every supporting character is genuinely distinctive and interesting; they are all, to borrow a line from children’s prose, “alive and glowing”. A rare feeling for contemporary series.

---

## Filming Begins on the Series Moshennik. Istoriya klouna with Lev Zulkarnaev

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/moshennik-istoriya-klouna-semki/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-06-10 (10 June 2026)
Work: “Moshennik. Istoriya klouna” is a work  Anton Fedorov.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, announcements
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/moshennik-istoriya-klouna-semki/

I see a project with Lev Zulkarnaev — I put it on my watchlist

Filming has started on the project ***Moshennik. Istoriya klouna*** («Мошенник. История клоуна», “The Swindler: A Clown’s Story”) from START and Premier (Russian streaming services). It is an adventure drama about a provincial circus performer who longs to avenge a deception suffered by someone close to him and joins a gang of phone scammers, and then becomes a brilliant con man himself. If you can’t beat them, lead them, as the saying goes.

I have long been waiting for new lead roles for Lev Zulkarnaev; I have missed them since [*She’s So Cool*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/ona-takaya-klassnaya-serial/) (*Ona takaya klassnaya*). The project’s director is Anton Fedorov, who is responsible for *Mir! Druzhba! Zhvachka!* (“Peace! Friendship! Bubblegum!”), so expectations are high on all sides. The cast will also include Kseniya Treyster, Efim Belosorochka, Evgeniya Simonova, Konstantin Murzenko, Vlad Tsenyov and many others. I am waiting eagerly.
