## Pluribus: The End of the World as a Chance to Achieve at Least Something in Your Own Eyes

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/pluribus-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-11-09 (9 November 2025); updated: 2025-12-27
Work: “Pluribus” is a 2025 series directed by Gordon Smith, Vince Gilligan.
Tags: series, science fiction, drama
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/pluribus-serial/

## 9 November 2025

I have watched the first episodes of [*Pluribus*](https://youtu.be/a6lzvWby9UE?si=KUNaXOPF7IBpFwfh), the science-fiction drama from Vince Gilligan (*Breaking Bad*, *Better Call Saul*) about a virus that turns the minds of all surviving people into a single whole. Except for the writer Carol, the heroine played by Rhea Seehorn, and a dozen or so other earthlings from different countries.

This is a vivid story that provokes complex emotions and questions about what you would do in the heroine’s place. That is precisely why the impeccable way it is all shot recedes into the background, its calibrated technique not eclipsing the moral dilemma.

After two episodes I am still mulling it over. Analogies come flooding in, from Covid and utopian hopes for ChatGPT to NPCs from video games and the trend for eco-friendly communication. This is exactly what makes the story many-layered and ambiguous, first of all thanks to its unpredictability, which is quite rare and, of course, motivates you to keep watching. It is separately interesting how the heroine’s desire to✨save the world✨ (in the traditions of American cinema) actually serves to compensate for her complexes about her inability to create a book that meets her own high standards. The end of the world becomes a chance to achieve at least something in her own eyes, and for that, of course, one can rise up against the entire world.

It is curious how Vince Gilligan, known first and foremost for the story of a man who, having fallen ill, begins a new life, has arrived at the story of a woman around whom the whole world has fallen ill, and who has no plans whatsoever to begin a new life)

## 15 November 2025

Episode 3 of [*Pluribus*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1070)

This is the first of the episodes whose script was not written by Vince Gilligan, and I was prepared for the previous pace to be gone. But not to that extent) Although, let us remember, *Breaking Bad* and *Better Call Saul* also wound up on their way to greatness quite slowly.

It seems that the series, like the representatives of the collective mind in the plot, has gone into energy-saving mode and the redistribution of resources for some future, as yet not entirely clear, goals.

Nor, incidentally, are the possible ways of continuing the story obvious. It is as if everything has stalled, and Carol asks none of the questions whose answers we viewers would very much like to know.

On the other hand, I have begun to enjoy the slightly absurd comedy we are being served. Showing the hundreds of people needed to run a supermarket where the “self-reliant and independent” heroine will buy everything for herself is funny and, moreover, very sobering for everyone on this side of the screen as to how everyday life is actually arranged.

## 22 November 2025

Episode 4 of [*Pluribus*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1085) flies by in an instant (and reminds you how pleasant it is to binge Vince Gilligan’s series).

It seems that the measure of cruelty the new collective world is prepared to go to was taken in the first 3 episodes. Now it is Carol’s turn, and she, it seems, has no intention of making allowances, either for herself or for the representatives of the new race. The unpredictability of her decisions and of the surrounding world’s reactions to them remains at the same level, and that is pleasant to watch. Especially considering the very legible humour at the expense of neural networks, famous for their neutral, meaningless answers)

I hope the second half of the season will give more understanding of the goals of the heroine and of the “uninfected” like her. But it is already clear that a second and even a third season are unavoidable.

## 28 November 2025

Episode 5 of [*Pluribus*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1109) on the whole almost fits into a quote from *A Clockwork Orange*: *“to have a glass of milk and do a bit of the old ultraviolence”* (only, naturally, with a “not”).

The story greatly benefits from going beyond the consequences of the apocalypse that has already happened and moving into unexplored territory. The second half of the season is exactly the time to do it. In particular, Carol’s investigation into the collective mind’s representatives’ love of milk seems set to spill over (pun not intended) into one of the season’s main plot twists, which will give impetus to future events.

Incidentally, I do not know whether it is intended or arises situationally, but the heroine’s attempts to lead the ranks of the scattered “survivors” are shown rather comically (and she reflects on this herself, too). There is no point waiting for a turning point when the series finally steps towards comedy or, on the contrary, loses all irony about the absurdity going on. As *Better Call Saul* and *Breaking Bad* taught us, Vince Gilligan combines all this superbly (I, at any rate, laughed without restraint at the moment with the drone that could not carry off the bag of rubbish).

## 16 December 2025

Episode 7 (the most uneventful at first glance) of [*Pluribus*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1138) could be labelled “sleeping-pill” content.

Were it not for a couple of genuinely sharp moments that demonstrate which of the heroes is prepared for what in this new world! If I ever have to explain the meaning of the term “slow burner”, I will probably refer to precisely this episode. Vince Gilligan is magnificent at this, as we remember from the first season of *Better Call Saul*, which was slow from beginning to end.

Here too nothing happens, yet in the background there are shifts of tectonic plates by the standards of plot and character development. The example of Carol and Manousos contrasts stagnation and regression with movement and overcoming oneself. The difference in motivations immediately becomes obvious: for whom it really was important to save the world, and for whom to become needed by someone in this new world. And from here on, obviously, the most interesting thing is to follow what endings the characters with such starting points will arrive at.

## 23 December 2025

What about [*Pluribus*?](https://t.me/kino_voice/1155)

It is unexpected (though understandable from the point of view of the series’ creators) that the meeting between Manousos and Carol is being put off for so long. Were it not for a couple of striking tendencies in these characters’ behaviour, episode 8 could even be called filler, for the exceptional self-containment of the two characters’ storylines.

But what obviously awaits us is an impressive season resolution with a meeting that should justify the need to wait for the continuation. Probably in the second season the struggle between methods of adapting to the new life will continue and will be even fiercer than Carol’s revolt at the very beginning. It is impressive how long the series’ authors manage to sustain the ambiguity of the new world order: another successful example of grey morality that contains arguments both for the infected and against them.

## 27 December 2025

The finale of [*Pluribus*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1165) is as imposing as an atomic bomb.

This is one of those episodes for which all the slow and uneventful episodes of the season were worth watching. In the finale, in a modest 50 minutes, everything is turned upside down twice, and in the density of its moral flip-flops it is simply an unsurpassed level.

Once again it turns out that man is an alien to man, even under the conditions of the end of the world. And where the line lies that cancels out cultural contrasts, we learn only in the last frames.

Episode 9 of *Pluribus* has the second-highest rating of the season on IMDb, 8.5 (against 9 for the pilot), and that is a good sign. I will await the second season with moderate impatience)

---

## Tunnel: The Plot Winds Like the Road Inside a Real Tunnel

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/tonnel-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-11-07 (7 November 2025); updated: 2025-12-01
Work: “Tunnel” is a 2025 series directed by Fluza Farkhshatova.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, thriller, crime
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/tonnel-serial/

## 7 November 2025

More details are emerging about [*Tunnel*](https://t.me/kino_voice/858).

Now we know not only that Elizaveta Boyarskaya’s heroine will be rescuing her husband, played by Sergei Gilev, somewhere on the border with Finland, but also that Finnish will be spoken in the series! Far from first in the queue of languages everyone dreams of learning, but that makes it all the more interesting to listen to. Here is how Boyarskaya learnt it:

> I can’t say I had a lot of scenes in Finnish, but I did have some. Now it seems that I learnt them endlessly, because Finnish is a very difficult language. I know German and English well, but Finnish is not like anything else; it belongs to the Finno-Ugric group of languages, which differs greatly from all the other groups. So it was as if I were learning Chinese. But it was important to me to do it well, so I really did cram the scenes in Finnish and practised with a coach. Those were the most nerve-racking and most difficult moments of the shoot

My inner linguist is intrigued.

## 1 December 2025

Meanwhile, [*Tunnel*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1060) has premiered on Kion (a Russian streaming service)

Judging by the first episodes, I want to say that you can watch it simply for Sergei Gilev as a funny father. But seriously, the thriller’s plot winds exactly like the road inside a real tunnel, and behind the resolution of one problem the origins of another immediately lurk.

Despite a somewhat TV-ish style of exposition and of introducing the characters, it is worth watching on until the action develops. There the world of characters is richer (Alexander Averin alone, giving off the vibes of a young Viktor Sukhorukov, is worth it), the motives are more varied, and there are more chances to hear Finnish)

A rare aesthetic while watching: catching the atmosphere of [*Peculiarities of the National Fishing*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/osobennosti-natsionalnoy-okhoty-1995/), where the characters accidentally ended up in Finland and did not immediately work out what was what (luckily, there was not a whiff of thriller there)

## The Magic District, Season 2: The Very Fairy Tale Adults Are Missing

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/volshebnyy-uchastok-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-11-06 (6 November 2025); updated: 2025-12-28
Work: “The Magic District” is a 2023 series directed by Stepan Gordeev.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, comedy, fantasy
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/volshebnyy-uchastok-serial/

## 6 November 2025

One of the best viewing sensations is to start the second season of a series having only just finished the first.

That is what I did with [*The Magic District*,](https://okko.tv/serial/volshebnyjj-uchastok) (*Volshebny uchastok*) having got acquainted with its universe right on the eve of the sequel’s premiere on Okko (the Russian streaming service). It was the best decision: from the first frame you do not want to climb out of the story for a minute, and the season finale gave no chance to relax at all. How pleasant it turned out not to have to wait 2 years for the continuation.

It would have been worth it in any case, though. The second season not only takes over all the merits of the first but multiplies them with interest. Lyokha Popov used to be simply funny in the Perm way; now he is also immortal, with all the gags that follow from it. The Gnome used to be simply a foul-mouthed dwarf (hard to believe, but he is my totem character one hundred percent); now he is not a gnome at all and not even foul-mouthed (and even cooler in his vocabulary, which I will be adding to my lexicon). There used to be the familiar Moscow; now there is a fairy-tale international St Petersburg (with jokes about mushrooms and salt, of which there is never too much (of the jokes)).

There is plenty to admire beyond the plot and the acting. In place are the fairy-tale looks of the characters, stunningly worked out by Anna Bashtova, the rhythmic direction of Stepan Gordeev, the coolest music and the charming atmosphere of the very fairy tale that adults are missing. Falling in love with this project is the best range of emotions you can experience at the end of 2025.

P.S.: As it happens, I also had the rare experience of watching *The Magic District* and *Realnye patsany* (“Real Lads”, the long-running Perm sitcom) in parallel, but I will write about that separately some time.

## 13 November 2025

I am still loving every minute of season 2 of [*The Magic District*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1050), and I have brought you a find!

Just now, for work, I got to listen to fresh, superb episodes of the podcast [Cinema is punk](https://cinemaispunk.mave.digital/) from the production company Mesto Sily (“Place of Power”), and it is the best companion for watching the series. Pay attention to 2 episodes:

- Stepan Gordeev (the series’ director) and Ilya Sobolev [discuss](https://cinemaispunk.mave.digital/ep-8) the role of the Gnome in *The Magic District*. They reveal who else auditioned for the part of the Foul-Mouth, how much a single shot with the character cost and which scene was filmed the very first (you really will not guess that one, because the moment turned out magnificent in the end). They also talk about a set of shot glasses with the character’s portrait that have an audio function for swearing at the drinker. Now I want one.

- Anna Bashtova, the costume designer for both seasons of *The Magic District*, [tells](https://cinemaispunk.mave.digital/ep-9) Stepan how she originally wanted to dress Baba Yaga, how old the fabric in Merlin’s robe is, why the Gnome is dressed in rags and what fly agarics have to do with it. By the way, her channel also has a lot of [fascinating material](https://t.me/kinocostume/32003) about the series. The coolest fact of the episode: real costumes from Alexei Balabanov’s films will appear on screen in the second season. How can you not look forward to the final episode?!

## 8 December 2025

And in [*The Magic District*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1050) everything is as fairy-tale as ever

I returned to watching after a couple of weeks and was very glad to see in episode 5 no fewer than two cool female characters: the Mermaid played by Valentina Mazunina (with the characteristic intonation of Valya from *Realnye patsany*) and a cameo by Anna Semenovich (in the plot, the singer has been captured by the wicked owner of a wish-granting pike). Once again I was reminded that the charm of the series lies, among other things, in little treats like these in the form of charismatic episodic characters)

I keep waiting to see how the story will approach New Year: after all, the last episode of the season is scheduled for 25 December, and the New Year mood will not create itself! I believe the authors have taken care of it: look, the pike, which is traditionally caught through a hole in the ice, was pulled out of the water in the middle of summer, so maybe some other winter folklore will come our way too.

P.S.: The wisdom tooth that utters those very wisdoms in the voice of Losyash (the moose from the animated series *Smeshariki*) is the peak. The whole episode I waited for it to say “my fairy-tale friend!”

## 28 December 2025

However detached [*The Magic District*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1139) may be from New Year themes, the series still managed to create a naively festive atmosphere for the season finale. The keys to success are these:

- Of course, there was no doing without ubiquitous New Year promo. It suits the series, as you can see from the poster.

- Perhaps Ilya Sobolev’s [greeting](https://t.me/mc2_prod/1884) “Happy New Year”, which was heard at the premiere, meant the new year of 1996 in the story, announced in the finale, rather than the literal holiday, as one might have thought. Well, the final change of era is more of a “Happy Old New Year!” (And yes, the 90s do not annoy me)

- We love and value New Year films precisely for their naive, life-affirming happy endings. There is one here, and in my opinion it is quite acceptable, if hasty by the standards of the action accelerating towards the resolution. One would like to hope that the wait for the next season will not drag on either)

## Peculiarities of the National Hunt: Digital Detox and Anti-Stress

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/osobennosti-natsionalnoy-okhoty-1995/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-11-03 (3 November 2025)
Work: “Peculiarities of the National Hunt” is a 1995 film directed by Aleksandr Rogozhkin.
Tags: rewatch, Russian cinema, comedy
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/osobennosti-natsionalnoy-okhoty-1995/

Well, here’s to the classics!

In October I was also studying the universe of Aleksandr Rogozhkin’s films: the three parts of *Peculiarities of the National Hunt* (in one of the films, of the National Fishing). I had seen fragments of these films on television long ago, but only now did I get round to watching them properly from start to finish. And not in vain: it was one of the best weekends of the month! If I were asked to name films synonymous with the words “digital detox” and “anti-stress”, I would choose these.

These anecdotes about the timeless face of the Russian soul, filmed with the utmost seriousness, surprisingly combine utterly carnivalesque humour with deeply existential philosophy. It is precisely in this paradox that some irrefutable sense of involvement in what happens on screen is born: both in terms of the fun shared with the characters and in terms of the general attitude to the absurdity of life. For this inimitable feeling you want to rewatch and rethink the films, plunging anew into a world without ranks or cares that flares up and fades somewhere on hunting trips in the forest (and also out of self-interest: to memorise for future use all the general’s pithy toasts, each beginning with the fundamental “Well…”)

## Every 88: The Quiet and Confident Impressiveness of What Is Happening

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/kazhdyy-88-2015/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-11-01 (1 November 2025)
Work: “Every 88” is a 2015 film directed by Darya Lebedeva.
Tags: Russian cinema, short films, parable
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/kazhdyy-88-2015/

Riding the wave of my admiration for [*You Drive Me Crazy*,](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/svodish-s-uma-2025/) I also watched one of director Darya Lebedeva’s short films, called *Every 88* («Каждый 88»).

It is a concise story about a young Soviet soldier who dies in battle and ends up in a mysterious place where a French athlete, a lady-in-waiting to an Austrian princess and many other figures from different times and nations have also gathered. They all stand in a long queue awaiting their destiny for the next life (which, of course, is assigned depending on the karma of the one they have lived). The artifice of this world is completely convincing, comic in places, and even melodramatic in a good way. But the main thing recognisable in the director’s style is the quiet and confident impressiveness of what is happening, whose meaning is centred not on the fantastical nature of the action but on its true significance when translated into the language of reality. It is cool that such a skill can be built into cinema, improving the result time after time.

---

## You Drive Me Crazy: The Feeling of Captivating Love Bottled in Film

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/svodish-s-uma-2025/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-10-29 (29 October 2025)
Work: “You Drive Me Crazy” is a 2025 film directed by Darya Lebedeva.
Tags: Russian cinema, rom-com, science fiction
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/svodish-s-uma-2025/

If you had no cinema plans for the coming evenings, urgently plan a trip to [*You Drive Me Crazy*.](https://youtu.be/39T_q4gt7HE?si=g9iPXzTNF-iuOeUm) (*Svodish s uma*) It is definitely worth catching.

I saw the film yesterday evening, and it is simply a find for any viewer. Director [Darya Lebedeva](https://t.me/lebedevadao) has made a stunning feature debut combining a convincing plot, the coolest performances from Mila Ershova and Yuri Nasonov, romance and humour in harmonious proportions, and a love of cinema that you feel through the screen. I have so many raptures that I will lay them out point by point (the film’s **rating of 8.5** on Kinopoisk will not let me lie)

- A fantastical element has never suited a romantic comedy so well, perhaps, since *Palm Springs*. The story of a guy and a girl who live in the same flat in different versions of the universe but see each other in the mirror and fall in love fits so well into the logic of the world of *You Drive Me Crazy* that no questions about it arise whatsoever. It is just as convincing as the plot of *Piter FM* (the 2006 St Petersburg rom-com) about two strangers who talk only by phone but can never manage to meet. The setting, by the way, is the same fateful St Petersburg, and it is very beautiful here. So even if you are on the side of realism, boldly decide to watch.

- After watching, I spent the whole evening and this morning discussing the details of what I had seen and decoding them. I have not plunged into analysing a film after watching like this for a long time, so you must take your favourite conversation partners to the screening. Everything matters here: the eccentric glasses of the hero, Vanya, Alisa’s fringe, the jokes about *Twilight* and cocktail recipes, the changed locks on the doors and the stickers stuck on the mirrors. The film is somewhat like an engaging quest that you are invited to complete with extremely likeable characters, who, incidentally, become better in the process, infecting the viewer with the same aspiration.

- From the moment you leave the auditorium your soul demands an immediate rewatch, and that is quite rare. You want to stretch *You Drive Me Crazy* out, prolong it, repeat it and not let it go. To convey the feeling, I will draw a parallel with Ray Bradbury’s *Dandelion Wine*. There he had “summer caught and bottled”, and here we have the feeling of captivating love and sincere closeness between two slightly lost people who deserve happiness, caught and bottled in film. How good that the film will most likely be released on the platform Start (the Russian streaming service), which is listed in the credits, and the chance to touch this story will always be there.

## Nazad v proshloe: An Audio Series About Time Travel

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/audioserial-nazad-v-proshloe/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-10-28 (28 October 2025)
Tags: подкасты, notes
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/audioserial-nazad-v-proshloe/

Podcast off-topic

As part of my work, I had a hand in the creation and release of a terrific audio series for lovers of history and time travel. It is called [*Nazad v proshloe*](https://zvuk.com/podcast/42757431) («Назад в прошлое», “Back to the Past”), with a film reference, naturally, because how else?

I listen to every episode before it is published and (despite years of listening to podcasts for work) I am amazed all over again at how well audio formats can work within cinematic storytelling. You literally listen to a film, or an episode of a series, filling in the picture in your own head, and it is indescribable. The podcast brings together professional actors and immersive sound design, and the plot surprises every time and lets you travel in your mind to one era or another. In short, when my eyes get tired of watching films, I will be listening to them in this podcast. The first episode is already out, and tomorrow the second one arrives too: just the right time to check it out.

That ultra-rare podcast recommendation on a film channel, at your service.

## Cashier: Four Heroines at Opposite Poles of Controlling Their Lives

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/obnalschik-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-10-27 (27 October 2025); updated: 2026-01-07
Work: “Cashier” is a 2025 series directed by Boris Akopov.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, crime
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/obnalschik-serial/

## 27 October 2025

Now here is news that makes me happy: from 13 November, Wink (a Russian streaming service) will release the series *Cashier* (*Obnalshchik*, “The Cash-Out Man”), a twisty story from Boris Akopov.

The series is set in 2013, and at the centre of the plot is the relationship between a father, Mikhail, and his son, Lyosha. After a string of failures, they start cashing out money together for dangerous people. The threat of a prison term, murders, betrayals: this is their new everyday life.

The cast includes Alexander Yatsenko, Elena Nikolaeva and Fyodor Kudryashov, and it was filmed in the Far East, which means that besides the crime plot we are also in for inimitable landscapes (I love that region very much myself, and I can vouch for its beauty). The protagonist, Mikhail, played by Yatsenko, is by all appearances my favourite type, the “bad good man”; here is what the actor himself says:

> Mikhail, like me, is not on familiar terms with pedagogy and parenting. Nevertheless, he tries to find common ground with his son, to come to an understanding. You know how it goes: you do one wrong thing, and because of it your whole life starts changing in the wrong direction. And then it is very hard to rewind, to admit you were wrong, to apologise and start changing something… Our series is about exactly that: how a person makes a mistake and tries to steer their way out of it. Mikhail is not a very good man or father, but his love for his son and his wife keeps him from turning into a criminal for good

Adding it to my watchlist, and waiting.

## 10 November 2025

[*Cashier*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1036) delights with its character posters and its [trailer](https://youtu.be/D02WcdPwhzA) (with some vibes of [*Daring*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/likhie-serial/))

Among the new developments: the premiere date has moved to 15 November. We will see the story of a father and son who pull off complex financial schemes for not the most pleasant clients as soon as the end of this week.

By the way, on the poster for Igor Mirkurbanov’s character, who is called the Fish King, there is a lamp in the foreground exactly like the one I have at home. Apparently, the series has to be watched exclusively by its light.

## 19 November 2025

So far [*Cashier*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1071) (*Obnalshchik*, “The Cash-Out Man”) looks to me like the sum of *Daring* (*Likhie*: crime in the Far East and Elena Nikolaeva as the mother of the family) and *Na avtomate* (“On Autopilot”, Boris Akopov’s previous project, where young people were also drawn into criminal adventures). But this does the series no harm at all!

Among other things, it has become clear why the poster puts such emphasis on the hand of Alexander Yatsenko’s character (those who have already seen the first episode will understand me). On the whole, the plot develops fairly quietly, yet grippingly, and, of course, wins you over. The criminal world here is heavily disguised as ordinary life, which is understandable: after all, this is not the 1990s but the 2010s, even if not the calmest of times. Besides, it is interesting to see what the theme of young people who have got their hands on easy money will lead to: the brothers in *Na avtomate* were also balancing before exactly that kind of moral choice.

## 10 December 2025

[*Cashier*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1094) has very competently picked up speed by the end of episode 5.

What is especially striking is the opposite poles at which the 4 main heroines stand when it comes to controlling their own lives and the lives of those around them. Two of them, Olga (Elena Nikolaeva) and Alyona (Sofya Lopunova), are not their own mistresses at all. Their life is the shadow of plans that the characters of Alexander Yatsenko and Fyodor Kudryashov are trying to carry out, and complete ignorance of what is going on at all.

Meanwhile the crime bosses Mama (Olga Tumaykina) and Katya (Elena Nesterova) are their reverse projection. The whole town is in their power, and any lie, if it happens at all, is cruelly punished. Not at all the situation the heroes’ beloveds find themselves in, with noodles hanging blatantly from their ears.

Perhaps one can even see a growth trajectory in this: maybe the current crime queens of Vostochny were once in that position too, and it was from exactly this point that they grew to the scale we are shown.

In Boris Akopov’s stories there is always something hidden deeper than it seems at first glance, so I have great faith in the female storylines.

## 7 January 2026

I have finished [*Cashier*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1143) and am, of course, impressed not so much by the finale as by the development of one particular heroine, Olga as played by Elena Nikolaeva.

In the middle of the season I wrote that she has no control over her life at all. Towards the end there was a 180-degree turn: weakness became her strength, an insinuating weapon with a gentle intonation. While her husband and son, the characters of Alexander Yatsenko and Fyodor Kudryashov, who lost none of their conviction, acted according to external circumstances and other people’s orders, she simply took the situation into her own hands.

To think she drove her guard (whose task was to kill the heroine a couple of hours later) to self-destruct! I am delighted: Boris Akopov came up with a heroine who outclassed all the gangsters of the Far East in a single scene. Maybe she is not much of a psychologist, but as a moral annihilator she worked at full capacity)

---

## Zhora Kryzhovnikov on Gaidai’s Comedies: Highlights of His Director’s Breakdown

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/kryzhovnikov-razbor-gaydaya/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-10-15 (15 October 2025)
Tags: Soviet cinema, analysis, comedy, film history
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/kryzhovnikov-razbor-gaydaya/

Zhora Kryzhovnikov has released a [new director’s breakdown](https://youtu.be/busSf9off_k?si=sLc8EfNnMnlzn6aL), this time of the work of Leonid Gaidai!

As [last time,](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/kryzhovnikov-razbor-sluzhebnyy-roman/) I have prepared a recap post with the main and most interesting points (and in brackets I have added bits of my own musings, relevant and otherwise)

- The most American of Soviet directors, Gaidai was guided largely by stunts, attractions and entertainment rather than by exploration. To examine his style, analysing one film is not enough, so the breakdown covers Gaidai’s work as a whole.

- The situation comedy Gaidai practised rests on holding the viewer (*uderzhanie*). It works through two other Russian “U”s: recognition (*uznavanie*) and surprise (*udivlenie*). But whereas for Ryazanov the plausibility of events mattered (hence, too, the inserts of semi-documentary street footage), Gaidai’s priorities are quite different. Most of the gags that work on surprise are completely fantastical: take, for instance, Gorbunkov’s trip to a capitalist country in *The Diamond Arm*. It does not correspond to reality, but it holds you thanks to the direction and the pacing.

- The pleasure of the attractions is inherently greater than the need to ask questions about what is going on. Paradoxically, the fantastical gags in Gaidai’s films tell us about the characters and win our trust. Therein lies the phenomenon of this director, which has not been repeated to this day.

- The concept of comedy as taught at school took shape in Stalin’s times. For details, see the book Kryzhovnikov recommends, *State Laughter: Stalinism, Populism, and Origins of Soviet Culture* («Госсмех. Сталинизм и комическое») (*it joins my reading list*). A Soviet person could only have the laughter of the victor, at swindlers and petty crooked officials. Soviet comedy always has a positive hero. Hence the stock perception of comedy as having an educational function. This is the reality Gaidai found himself in at the start of his career.

- Gaidai is a unique director who, while outwardly belonging to Soviet comedy, created pure entertainment.

- Gaidai’s first films, *Zhenikh s togo sveta* («Жених с того света», “The Groom from the Other World”) and *Trizhdy voskresshiy* («Трижды воскресший», “Thrice Resurrected”), were very hard ordeals for the director, which he disliked recalling for the rest of his life (*and we have practically never heard of them*).

- Gaidai adored silent cinema. Kryzhovnikov is also of the opinion that a film should be understandable even with the sound off (*an evening’s entertainment: I will rewatch* Gorko! *(«Горько!», “Bitter!”, Kryzhovnikov’s 2013 wedding comedy) with this thought in mind*).

- Gaidai worked with a stopwatch: he timed the gap from one laugh moment to the next, which is exactly why, 60 years on, we still watch his films with interest.

- The director gravitated towards the short form: this format grabs attention faster. His feature films often consist of several segments, and long films made him uncomfortable because of potential viewer fatigue.

- Gaidai’s concept of situation comedy is safe entertainment. In his films there is no real pain, nobody dies and nobody walks out on anyone. The basic principle is “beautiful women + funny men”. Every element of Gaidai’s comic style is unique and based on his favourite films (for example, the references to Buster Keaton). Perhaps one day Russian cinema will produce someone to carry on Gaidai’s work.

---

## My Mom’s Penguins, Season 2: The Bet on the Novelty Effect Paid Off

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/pingviny-moey-mamy-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-10-14 (14 October 2025); updated: 2025-11-26
Work: “My Mom’s Penguins” is a 2021 series directed by Natalya Meshchaninova, Nadezhda Stepanova.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, dramedy
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/pingviny-moey-mamy-serial/

## 14 October 2025

*My Mom’s Penguins* (*Pingviny moey mamy*) is coming back.

Kion (a Russian streaming service) promises to release the second season of the series this very autumn, so there is not long left to wait.

Makar Khlebnikov’s character Gosha has grown up: he performs stand-up, quarrels with his girlfriend (Elizaveta Ishchenko) and earns money to rent a flat. His parents are absorbed in moving to a new house and are expecting their 6th child. And keeping an eye on his growing brothers and sisters falls, of course, to Gosha.

I am really looking forward to seeing how Liza Ishchenko fits into the team, all the more so since she herself is a fan of the project:

> I enjoyed watching the first season of *My Mom’s Penguins* and am a big fan of it. The second season attracted me because I could try myself in a new facet, with a new story and with a magical team that was creating a very interesting project with love. My heroine Vika is a fiery combo of two elements, fire and water, so I plunged in and became completely saturated with her on set. I was changing before everyone’s eyes, and the people close to me on set were surprised at what a volcanic character I could show. I had long wanted to work with Makar, because we have known each other for a long time, and, as it happens, the stars aligned!

## 26 November 2025

Are you watching the continuation of [*My Mom’s Penguins*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1042)? I have started, and so far I am getting used to the numerous changes.

If the bet was on the novelty effect, it paid off. Now Gosha’s step-brothers and step-sister are the owners and catalysts of quite independent storylines, which widens the context compared with the first season. Obviously, the range of themes will grow too: we will be worrying not only about the family’s own son, at any rate. By the way, the change of location does the series good as well: almost everyone in the second season sets off on a journey one way or another (as always, not only geographically but also towards their true self).

Gosha’s stand-up was shown at the very beginning of episode 1, and thanks for that: it is nice to return to that “room”. The whole season is already out; I hope they carry on in the same spirit.

## Comeback: The Air of an Era That Breathes Genuine Youth Through the Screen

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/kambek-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-10-11 (11 October 2025); updated: 2025-11-16
Work: “Comeback” is a 2025 series directed by Dinar Garipov.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, 2000s
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/kambek-serial/

## 11 October 2025

I have got round to [*Comeback*](https://www.kinopoisk.ru/series/6605654/) (*Kambek*), an ultra-atmospheric series with Alexander Petrov as a homeless man who has lost his memory.

The action takes place in the 2000s, and the air of the era literally breathes through the screen with some kind of genuine youth. This atmosphere is intensified by the teenage protagonists: strong, brave, wise in their own way. And it is all scored with tracks by Mujuice, who always reaches right to the depths of the soul. And the plot, of course, from episode to episode emphasises something unhackneyed about friendship, kindness to one’s neighbour and to oneself. Simple and tasteful.

Watching it, I felt things long forgotten since [*Mir! Druzhba! Zhvachka!*,](https://t.me/kino_voice/13) (“Peace! Friendship! Bubblegum!”, the 1990s-set series) so I am with this series to the end.

## 18 October 2025

I continue to ~~watch~~ adore [*Comeback*](https://t.me/kino_voice/997)

The fourth episode of the series is a perfect example of a situation where the vertical plot of an episode complements the overall horizontal structure of the story so organically that it is even hard to separate them. Gratitude to the creators and to [@russian_c0de](https://t.me/russian_c0de) for such craftsmanship, of course.

The series is at its midpoint and is very competently gaining momentum. The [record](https://t.me/kinopoisk_Industry/5558) viewing figures say so eloquently. Such demand, it seems to me, can be explained by interest in the chosen era. We all, to one degree or another (especially younger viewers), came out of the 2000s, out of that culture, that reference point in our worldview and sense of self. And recalling one’s relative youth is always absorbing.

## 20 October 2025

I am separately enjoying the aesthetics of the school the heroes of [*Comeback*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1013) attend

For me these are home landscapes. The main value is that it is an *ordinary* school (even if that came about only because of the period: in 2004 all schools were like that). I studied at exactly this type of school, and my eye rejoices at the familiar layout of the classrooms with those peeling wooden chairs (which forever snagged your tights, the girls will understand me), the worn linoleum, the wooden shelving, the wide windowsills and the chaotic plants on them. The canteen is a little bigger than in the still from the series, but with the same serving line of metal vessels with red lettering. In my last years of school, the chalkboards were replaced by whiteboards and then partly by electronic ones, but everything around remained as it was)

These days you hardly ever see such schools on screen, certainly not in stories about our time: everywhere there is bound to be a swimming pool, a canteen with a buffet like a hotel, and ultra-fashionable renovations. Such schools really do exist, but schools of the old type exist and operate in parallel (I went to mine last year, and the authenticity is intact). And it is very pleasant to recognise on screen a piece of one’s personal youth, which, it turns out, can even serve as a film set.

## 23 October 2025

Time for crazy theories

After the powerful, practically journalistic investigation that Yura from [*Comeback*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1013) carried out in the latest episode, I cannot stop thinking that he could have grown up to be Yury Dud*\* (the journalist and YouTube interviewer) in his series’ universe.

**✅** Born in the late 1980s
**✅** Adores football
**✅** The name and the physical resemblance speak for themselves
**✅** Most likely, Yura is a humanities type (we saw him copying maths from Ptakha)

How do I unsee this?

\* Yury Dud* has been designated a “foreign agent” in Russia

## 31 October 2025

In the sixth episode of [*Comeback*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1013) many storylines are very neatly written off, precisely to place the emphasis on the new input in the form of Alexey Chadov’s mysterious character. Obviously it is he who will be one of the main protagonists in the two final episodes, and for that a little extra artistic and running-time space is needed.

Separately pleasing is the quotation of a scene from the film *Brother*. If you remember, at a certain point Danila there tried to stand up for Sveta, the tram driver, against her husband, who was beating her. Having neutralised the man, Danila asked her to leave with him, but she stayed with her spouse, who was suffering from a bullet in his leg and would obviously go on beating her. The same thing, almost frame for frame, was repeated in *Comeback*, and, one might say, has already reached the level of an archetypal plot.

By the way, I am watching the series very attentively in order to record every episode in a Kinopoisk [feature](https://www.kinopoisk.ru/media/article/4011978/); if you find yourself pondering the details, drop in.

## 16 November 2025

And the best adornment of the finale of [*Comeback*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1043) is the [news](https://t.me/kinopoisk_soon/20435) of a second season of the series.

In the last episode the concentration of events reached an off-the-scale level, but, pleasingly, not one of the storylines suffered for it. Though I preferred the first half of the story, where, first, the kids seemed to still have everything ahead of them (😭), and second, there was enough time to reflect on each event. But the last episodes have their own drive too, combined with the feeling of a departing era, of a great adventure and the carefree early 2000s.

What will I expect from season 2? Updated images of the kids (in particular, the development of Dasha’s affairs of the heart with various candidates and with Petya, who vanished as suddenly as he appeared). A non-glossy look of the late 00’s, in the series’ tradition, naturally. And the normalisation of Kompot’s life: showing the hardships of a homeless man’s life is half the job; far harder is to reflect honestly the difficulties of his socialisation and of overcoming the stigma trailing from his former status.

It is cool that the project has deservedly got a continuation, and one really does want to wait for it.

* Yury Dud (Дудь Юрий Александрович) has been designated a “foreign agent” by Russia’s Ministry of Justice (listed on 15 April 2022).

## Lighthouse: A Multilayered Reflection on the Nature of Guilt, Grief and Family Trauma

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/mayak-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-10-09 (9 October 2025)
Work: “Lighthouse” is a 2025 series directed by Ilya Malakhova.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, drama
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/mayak-serial/

Okko (the Russian streaming service) and the production company Sreda have stunned everyone again.

The closing series, *Lighthouse* (*Mayak*), is
a choice of jeweller’s precision to end the festival on the highest note, on the rise.

The work is adorned by Mikhail Turbin’s beautiful script, the piercing performances of Evgeny Kuntsevich, Sergei Gilev and Yulia Snigir, and Natalya Makarova’s camerawork, lively, mobile and in sync with the lives of the characters in the frame. It is all brought together by Ilya Malakhova’s direction. Thanks to this, the story of high-school student Egor, who looks after his younger brother with cerebral palsy instead of his parents, who have escaped into their work, becomes not just a grim tale of human misfortune but a multilayered reflection on the nature of guilt, grief, family trauma and living through loss.

The real discovery of the series is Evgeny Kuntsevich. Over 2 episodes this actor played almost everything: tender love for his younger brother, sincerity in standing up for himself, the sparkle in his eyes from first love, carelessness, responsibility, the devastation of loss, anger, despair and hopelessness. I am sure the next episodes will bring still other, unexplored facets of emotion.

Okko’s general producer Gavr Gordeev says that the basis of the platform’s philosophy is an empathetic attitude towards the viewer. With mutual empathy, I will be waiting for the premiere of the series *Lighthouse* in 2026.

---

## The Good Life: An Imagistic Attempt at Adapting The Blue Cup

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/khoroshaya-zhizn-2025/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-10-08 (8 October 2025)
Work: “The Good Life” is a 2025 film directed by Tatyana Rakhmanova.
Tags: Russian cinema, adaptation, festival films, drama
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/khoroshaya-zhizn-2025/

*The Good Life* (*Khoroshaya zhizn*) is a film I was waiting for because of Serafima Goshchanskaya, and she is wonderful here (although she has frustratingly little screen time)

The story, based on *Golubaya chashka* («Голубая чашка», “The Blue Cup”) by Arkady Gaidar (the classic Soviet children’s writer), does not unravel all the mysteries of the original text (once again, [an interweaving of different particles of culture](https://t.me/kino_voice/973)). For me this story is a very powerful impression from childhood, powerful precisely because it is not fully understood, and I expected the film to reveal at least some of the plot’s secrets. That does not seem to have happened, although I would call the film a very cool imagistic attempt at adapting this text (and a reminder to reread it).

## Above Eternal Rest: A Difficult Film You Want to Keep Thinking About

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/nad-vechnym-pokoem-2025/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-10-08 (8 October 2025)
Work: “Above Eternal Rest” is a 2025 film directed by Svetlana Proskurina.
Tags: Russian cinema, festivals, drama
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/nad-vechnym-pokoem-2025/

The final film of the competition programme, Svetlana Proskurina’s *Above Eternal Rest* (*Nad vechnym pokoem*), very much mirrors [*My Son*,](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/moy-syn-2025/) which we watched first. This premiere has every right to be called a contemporary *Cargo 200* (Alexei Balabanov’s film) mixed with *Crime and Punishment*. Only, whereas before evil was committed shamelessly in an open room, now it is hidden under the floorboards, with people going mad from complicity, from landing in a “random hell”, as the director put it, and that is something else.

The story of a mother and son bound by one terrible secret does not let you take your eyes off the everydayness of murder in the name of salvation, not even a crime, that word sounds too formal here. At the same time it is hard to condemn Rita, the heroine played by Masha Leonova: she is not a villainess, not a killer and not a bad person. She too is a victim. And understanding this true state of affairs in the story is what weighs on the viewer most of all.

A difficult film that you want to keep thinking and reasoning about. Masha Leonova is a wonderful actress whom one would like to see in such subtle roles more often. She showed a heroine who to the very end makes you doubt whether she has gone mad, or turned savage from indifference, or coldly calculated her deed. Possibly the best female role of the festival.

---

## Yura Was Here: A Film About Beautiful People, Beauty of the Soul and Love for One’s Neighbour

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/zdes-byl-yura-2025/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-10-08 (8 October 2025); updated: 2026-02-05
Work: “Yura Was Here” is a 2025 film directed by Sergey Malkin.
Tags: Russian cinema, festivals, music
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/zdes-byl-yura-2025/

## 8 October 2025

*Yura Was Here* (*Zdes byl Yura*) is an unimaginably beautiful film about beautiful people, beauty of the soul and love for one’s neighbour, which saves first of all the one who loves. Do not think this is some sentimental sweetness: on the contrary, the film is punk, dynamic, out of the ordinary.

Onto the heads of the heroes, young musicians, lands Yura (Konstantin Khabensky), the uncle of one of the guys, who because of a birth injury can neither speak nor live independently at all. To the heroes’ difficulties with their neighbour in a communal flat and their attempts to break onto the big stage is added the care of a relative who at first seems to be needed by nobody. In time it is he who becomes the most important person for all the participants in the story.

The artistic world of the film is filled with music, colours and details that bring everything to life. I recognised in the frame, for instance, the cool café Chifanka in Moscow’s Kitay-Gorod)

I cannot help confessing my love for the songs of the band Kick Chill as performed by Kuzma Kotrelev; the creators promise to release a separate soundtrack. This, in my opinion, is the hit of the film festival, as the song “Allo, Marina” from the film *God rozhdeniya* (“Year of Birth”) once was. Things are fine with references here too: at the moment the candles on the cake are lit, for example, someone says the phrase “Everyone out of the Gloom”, for which Khabensky’s character from *Night Watch* is famous.

I will go and watch it a second time as soon as it is in cinemas: from 5 February, courtesy of [@bosforpictures](https://t.me/bosforpictures) and [@volgafilms](https://t.me/volgafilms).

## 18 December 2025

**Found: the best way to start your 2026 in film**

The one that did not make the top lists for 2025 (simply because it has not come out yet) is the wonderful film [*Yura Was Here*](https://t.me/kino_voice/967): utterly astonishing in every respect, from the plot and dialogue to the directing, camerawork and editing, and it also won the hearts of everyone present at Mayak 2025 (the Russian film festival in Gelendzhik).

Luckily, the team at the Bosfor studio is already preparing for the release: it starts on 5 February, and tickets for the first audience premiere on 25 January can be bought [right now](https://t.me/bosforpictures/609). Do not miss it: it is a wonderful way to start your film year on a high note)

When we draw up the top lists of Russian films for 2026, *Yura* will be among the first, I guarantee it.

## 5 February 2026

And from today [*Yura Was Here*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1128) is in cinemas: a film that has kept me in raptures ever since Mayak, the Russian film festival in Gelendzhik (that was in October, mind you)

I [wrote](https://t.me/kino_voice/967) about the film right after seeing it, and today I have put together a short list of reasons to see this film on the big screen:

- Kuzma Kotrelev singing (if you know [what](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/mezhdu-nami-khimiya-serial/) I mean) and wonderful music all round
- An impressive performance by Konstantin Khabensky. You seriously will not recognise him.
- Lively dialogue sprinkled with contemporary memes (mostly improvised!)
- The kindest humour without a single cloying note
- Wonderful details you want to take a close look at, from the interiors of the communal flat to the side streets of Kitay-Gorod
- Plenty of reasons to smile gratefully at this film after watching it (and perhaps to wipe away a tear)

I am sure that after watching it, everyone will be able to put together their own personal list of reasons to recommend this film to others.

## Tied Up: A Cinematic Celebration of Animation, Sincerity and Kindness

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/na-vybros-2025/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-10-07 (7 October 2025)
Work: “Tied Up” is a 2025 film directed by Konstantin Bronzit.
Tags: animation, Russian cinema, festivals
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/na-vybros-2025/

Konstantin Bronzit’s *Tied Up* (*Na vybros*, “For the Dump”) is a real cinematic celebration of animation, sincerity and kindness. In the spirit of Pixar, but with a native soul.

The story of things thrown out onto the rubbish heap which, just like people, want to be needed and useful, touches you so much precisely because this thought is close to anyone. They desperately try to reach a paradise, even if a rubbish-dump one, and how can you not understand them?

The animated film gives the feeling of a true dramedy, provoking laughter and tears at the same time. The humour is built on paradox, so it works without fail. Just consider the joke by the rat that feeds on books, to the effect that Pasternak is a bit bland. At times it even feels like a dystopia in the spirit of Pelevin, but only in its positive manifestations.

Konstantin Bronzit, who worked on the film for 5 years, modestly laughs it off: it is only a children’s cartoon, he says) But the message about the eco-friendly treatment not only of rubbish but, first and foremost, of living people is unmistakable.

In cinemas from 20 November, an unequivocal recommandation.

---

## Nouvelle Vague: A True Declaration of Love for Cinema

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/novaya-volna-2025/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-10-07 (7 October 2025)
Work: “Nouvelle Vague” is a 2025 film directed by Richard Linklater.
Tags: world cinema, European cinema, film history
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/novaya-volna-2025/

Richard Linklater’s [*Nouvelle Vague*](https://t.me/kino_voice/899) is a very structured and rhythmic account of the making of Jean-Luc Godard’s famous *Breathless*.

Every character is introduced, the context is set, just sit back and enjoy — thanks to an easy immersion in the everyday life of French filmmakers, the humour of their discussions lands quickly and delights. It is a real journey into the French New Wave for everyone who decides to watch the film.

A special delight is the casting. Each of the actors is as convincing as the real person behind the role and comes across as almost documentary. But I was especially won over by the actor playing Jean-Paul Belmondo, Aubry Dullin.

In short, the result is a true declaration of love for cinema — you can share the feeling in cinemas from 6 November.

---

## Transparent Lands: A Film That Demands Heightened Attention from the Viewer

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/prozrachnye-zemli-2025/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-10-07 (7 October 2025)
Work: “Transparent Lands” is a 2025 film directed by Dmitry Davydov.
Tags: Russian cinema, festivals, drama
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/prozrachnye-zemli-2025/

*Transparent Lands* (*Prozrachnye zemli*) is a film that demands heightened attention from the viewer, if not a second viewing.

The story of three old men living in solitude in a traditional village (outstanding work by the production designers), as if outside time, unfolds practically without words. They while away the time with tea, the banya (steam bath) and cupping jars, and hunting, until they fish out of the pond a man frozen to the state of glass. In the hut he thaws, comes back to life and even starts baking bread, presenting it to the old men as a real miracle (and motivating a wonderful scene of celebration in the snowy night). Only after his disappearance does the life of the village’s inhabitants change.

Contrary to its title, the film cannot be called transparent. It starts a discussion of the fear of death, the preservation of memory and the philosophy of life. Director Dmitry Davydov gradually leads us into the world of a dying village, showing the process of its passage into a space of transparent memories, where the whole village circles in the eternal round dance of the ancestors, no longer belonging to our world, just like the life reflected in the picture.

---

## Scenes of Friendly Ties: An Atmosphere Film Woven from Fragments of Friendship

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/kartiny-druzheskikh-svyazey-2025/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-10-06 (6 October 2025)
Work: “Scenes of Friendly Ties” is a 2025 film directed by Sonya Rayzman.
Tags: Russian cinema, festivals, dramedy
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/kartiny-druzheskikh-svyazey-2025/

*Scenes of Friendly Ties* (*Kartiny druzheskikh svyazey*) is an atmosphere film woven from fragments of friendship and the leisure of film-industry pals. I would call it “fan service for insiders”, with local memes about the woes of film people, the Lev Zulkarnaev type and the specifics of theatre schools)

The plot about the departure of one of the friends (Alexander Pal) serves as a background rather than an engine of the plot, and the pals’ professional conflicts turn out to be more interesting. In this respect the picture sometimes falls apart into episodic sketches, which, however, is no great problem, because each of them is like a small dramedy, complete independently of the main line.

The only thing that raises questions is the scene with the cat. The thing is, the film begins with him being put down (morally devastating for Maria Karpova’s heroine and for all the viewers), although no illness is stated. Later we see a flashback of how the cat was found while the heroes were studying at theatre school, and that was not so many years ago, so the picture acquires an even more paradoxical meaning. It is clear that the cat’s death is a metaphor for the end of the heroes’ relationship, but a very cruel one.

---

## Fire Boy: An Uneven Film, but Alive and Striving Towards the Light

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/ognennyy-malchik-2025/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-10-06 (6 October 2025)
Work: “Fire Boy” is a 2025 film directed by Nadezhda Mikhalkova.
Tags: Russian cinema, festivals, drama
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/ognennyy-malchik-2025/

Nadya Mikhalkova’s *Fire Boy* (*Ognenny malchik*) is an uneven film, but alive and striving towards the light.

The story of the feelings of a young man before whose eyes a person accidentally burned to death (that very “fire boy”) grips the attention on several themes at once. There is the lack of contact with his mother (comically consonant with the lack of mobile reception for most of the film), the danger of everyday indifference, and a search for himself with a touch of mysticism. In this respect Denis Kosikov paradoxically precisely conveys every facet of his hero’s state. I can say the same of Bogdan Goloshchuk, a most vivid actor whose character appears briefly at the very beginning in order to set the tone of the whole film at once.

I find a lot in common between the themes of *Fire Boy* and Alexander Gorchilin’s *Acid*, which stated a similar problem of indifference and a subsequent attempt to forgive oneself with the pithy phrase “if you want to jump, jump”. And that is why the film, despite its rough edges nearer the finale,  rather hit home with me.

---

## Skladki: An Uplifting Body Horror About the Beauty of the Human Body

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/skladki-2025/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-10-06 (6 October 2025)
Work: “Skladki” is a 2025 film directed by Katerina Skakun.
Tags: Russian cinema, short films, festival films
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/skladki-2025/

The short film competition is over: I am extremely fond of one of the films, so that is the one I will write about here. As for the rest, read about them in the piece that will be here in a couple of days)

The film *Skladki* («Складки», “Folds”) is an uplifting body horror, as the director Katerina Skakun herself put it. And it really is a very charming story about the beauty of the human body, of life and of love, which can be literally all-consuming (and all-saving too). Whether to be frightened of it or to embrace this life-giving feeling is for each of us to decide.

In the plot, an enthusiastic tour guide and a female chiropractor fall in love, but their relationship does not fall into place as smoothly as it might have. But the main thing is how it all happens, and that is what the film is worth watching for. Recommended for lovers of magical realism, of Suzdal (the old Russian town) and of the atmosphere of love at first sight.

---

## Fireworks in the Afternoon: The Very Film Worth Travelling to Festivals For

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/feyerverki-dnem-2025/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-10-05 (5 October 2025)
Work: “Fireworks in the Afternoon” is a 2025 film directed by Nina Volova.
Tags: Russian cinema, festivals, dramedy
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/feyerverki-dnem-2025/

*Fireworks in the Afternoon* (*Feyerverki dnyom*) is the very film worth travelling to festivals for. Alive, sparkling and elusively beautiful, like those very fireworks set off in the afternoon.

An airy, realistic story about three sisters trying to save the family nest from being sold is an extremely successful feature debut by Nina Volova. A drama on the edge of non-stop laughter and bitter tears, it has also managed to absorb the mood of Chekhov’s texts, both *Three Sisters* and *The Cherry Orchard*.

At the same time the film steps with one foot into the territory of a conversation about the mysterious Russian soul: the estranged gaze is provided by Wang Bing’s character, a Chinese entrepreneur who is at first very calculating. His gaze largely creates the comic sensation of examining yourself in a mirror, but a good-natured one, open to the new.

The team was applauded for about 10 minutes; I filmed a couple of moments. It is so far the best film I have seen in the programme, and I will very much look forward to its release so I can show it to everyone.

---

## Lermontov: A Journey Through Time to What Does Not Change with Time

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/lermontov-2025/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-10-05 (5 October 2025); updated: 2025-10-16
Work: “Lermontov. Doomsday” is a 2025 film directed by Bakur Bakuradze.
Tags: Russian cinema, biopic, festivals
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/lermontov-2025/

## 5 October 2025

And in general [*Lermontov*](https://t.me/kino_voice/941) is an astonishing journey through time to what does not change with time.

From the first frames the picture envelops you in the texture of the era and the place, literally letting you touch a way of life and of thinking. We slow down together with the static camera, which does not hurry after the characters’ movements but records the overall picture almost impassively. Like fate, which is often woven from fatal mistakes.

In the poet’s last day before the duel there is nothing that would betray the singularity of the moment. On the contrary, this day seems to interest everyone except the protagonist. And Ilya Ozolin excellently conveys an ironic indifference to himself and the world, laconically and caustically joking against the backdrop of a village pastoral.

This film can be called a kind of antipode of *Prorok* (“The Prophet”, the Pushkin musical biopic). All they have in common is turning to the biographies of poetic geniuses. In everything else *Lermontov* is quieter, more modest, more realistic and more everyday, especially as regards the terrible moment of a senseless death. But death is not the end of the reflection, and Bakuradze places his full stop far more elegantly. Perhaps that is exactly why the film stands outside the competition: it is hard to judge the eternal truth about the senselessness of violence.

Catch it in cinemas from [@volgafilms](https://t.me/volgafilms) and [@k24films](https://t.me/k24films) from 16 October.

## 16 October 2025

From today Bakur Bakuradze’s beautiful [*Lermontov*](https://t.me/volgafilms/6926) is in cinemas. Following my [hot recommendation from Mayak](https://t.me/kino_voice/942) (the film festival in Gelendzhik), I also want to highlight one significant detail for everyone who has yet to get acquainted with the picture.

I mean the epilogue scene. It is a very inventively created version, by the director, of an alternative universe in which everything could have turned out differently. Pay attention to the last scene of the film, where Lermontov, in his usual manner, sets up a prank on the husband of a lady who has been playing billiards with him. Everything is arranged so that (given a certain temperament in the husband) there would be every right to challenge the poet to a duel. But that does not happen. In this case what wins is the trust between the spouses, a sense of self-worth, the humanist principles of the value of life. In a word, everything that saves not only poets but people in general.

---

## My Son: A Picture Rich in Symbols That Need Deciphering

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/moy-syn-2025/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-10-05 (5 October 2025)
Work: “My Son” is a 2025 film directed by Vyacheslav Klevtsov.
Tags: Russian cinema, drama, festivals
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/moy-syn-2025/

The programme (largely devoted to family ties) opens with the film *My Son* (*Moy syn*). It is the feature debut of director Vyacheslav Klevtsov. The leads are Yulia Snigir, Leon Kemstach and Pavel Tabakov (who presented the film together with the crew).

The picture, designed in a minimalist, cold way, is rich in symbols, and you need to go and see it ready to decipher them. Before us is a successful lawyer who has lied herself into a corner with the whole world and with herself: at first she lies even to her psychologist. Her son is someone else’s son. Her home is an eternal dusty building site. Her appearance is a mask that she managed to take off too late. Yulia Snigir looks extremely convincing in this angular vacuum, without arousing a drop of sympathy in the audience. Her heroine, only on losing her son, realises that she has lost herself. She is convinced of it when she is also rejected by an admirer blind to her sins. And bribery and bought verdicts make an excellent background.

As one of the film’s key young characters says: “Our generation weeps for the sins of yours.” The conflict of fathers and children is resolved here in something of a draw. In the words of the creators, “the heroine finds strength in the ability to experience emotions”. Where the young generation finds its strength is for the viewers to decide.

---

## The “General’s Ticker” Meme: How a Mikhalkov Scene Became an Internet Phenomenon

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/mem-generalskie-kotly/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-09-28 (28 September 2025)
Work: “Burnt by the Sun 2: Citadel” is a work  Nikita Mikhalkov.
Tags: Russian cinema, pop culture, notes
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/mem-generalskie-kotly/

I cannot pass by the “general’s ticker” meme («генеральские котлы», literally “the general’s cauldrons”, criminal slang for a wristwatch).

You have probably come across the scene from *Burnt by the Sun 2: Citadel* somewhere in vertical videos over the past month. Paradoxically, the meme spread because the incredible pathos of the source scene met the absurdity and post-irony of today’s memes. So to speak, the “wild general’s ticker” has become “the general’s ticker now”.

A scene this full of meme material, with a bandit whose look resembles Grigory Leps (the Russian pop singer), a Wolverine glove on Nikita Mikhalkov’s hand and lines that sound like ready-made quotations, was bound to become an internet phenomenon sooner or later.

On this overcast autumn evening I am attaching my favourite version: nothing superfluous, only the “general’s ticker” and the music from the series *The Kitchen* (the hit Russian sitcom).

By the way, put a **🐳** if you are interested in breakdowns of film memes, and drop your favourite film memes in the comments.

## Ruslan and Lyudmila: Interviews with the Team for Kinopoisk

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/ruslan-i-lyudmila-intervyu-s-komandoy/
Author: Betsy Isakova

Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/ruslan-i-lyudmila-intervyu-s-komandoy/

It would seem too early to be waiting for the premieres of 2027, but I already am.

It is all because of the charming team of *Ruslan and Lyudmila* («Руслан и Людмила. Волшебное путешествие»), who [told me about the shoot](https://www.kinopoisk.ru/news/4011823/)[,](https://t.me/FBChu/48186) and so vividly that I am already dreaming of watching it all. An acting task of genius, in my opinion!) And whom the screenwriter Denis Danilov pictured in the role of Ruslan I will not even hint at: let it remain a bonus for those who read the [piece](https://www.kinopoisk.ru/news/4011823/)

## Nanny Oksana: Faithful to the Style of 2000s Series

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/nyanya-oksana-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-09-23 (23 September 2025)
Work: “Nanny Oksana” is a 2025 series directed by Evgeniya Abdel-Fattah.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, sitcom, 2000s
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/nyanya-oksana-serial/

Some things never change: the funniest jokes in series about nannies in rich families are invariably delivered by the butler.

I mean [*Nanny Oksana*](https://youtu.be/ji9PJSF7Ys0?si=p-FVD2OhCDGTw0Bq) (*Nyanya Oksana*), which premiered the day before at the Khudozhestvenny (a historic Moscow cinema). The series wins you over with its faithfulness to the style of 2000s series (even more so than the new *Moscow Does Not Believe in Tears*). Here you have interstitials in the style of the opening titles between scenes, the cartoonish personalities of the children, and the implausibly miraculous way the nanny lands a job in a rich man’s family. Such naivety can be considered the plot’s calling card, and you can unerringly find it in every frame.

Everything that happens is freshened up by the abundance of jokes about the hallmarks of the Russian TV channel Pyatnitsa (“Aren’t you that chef who drives all the show’s contestants to hysterics? I adore you!”), sprinklings of modern clichés like “harassment”, and a cunning streak in the head of the family that the source material did not have. The only thing is that the local Zhanna Arkadyevna (the nanny’s rival in *My Fair Nanny*, the 2000s Russian version of *The Nanny*) still lags behind in bitchiness, but that may be a matter of time, and after the premiere on 29 September it is all still to come.

---

## One Call Bar: A Chamber Reflection on Fixating on Missed Chances

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/bar-odin-zvonok-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-09-22 (22 September 2025); updated: 2025-10-24
Work: “One Call Bar” is a 2025 series directed by Sergey Filatov.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, supernatural
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/bar-odin-zvonok-serial/

## 22 September 2025

All episodes of [*One Call Bar*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/dva-seriala-s-daniloy-kozlovskim/) (*Bar “Odin zvonok”*) will be released on 1 October!

After the news that the project was coming back, the premiere date did not keep us waiting long, and that is great. The crew’s view of the project adds particular interest. Here is what director Sergey Filatov says:

> This is a story about regret. We often regret what we have done and, perhaps even more often, what we have not done. Some things cannot be undone — that is the whole horror and beauty of life: it is momentary. It is important to remind yourself of that sometimes.

It is good that the series is coming out after all, and there will be nothing to regret about it.

## 24 October 2025

By the way, [*One Call Bar*](https://t.me/kino_voice/909) works very well watched in one sitting!

The project’s high concept (a mysterious bar where an ironically burned-out bartender is always happy to offer a call to the other world in exchange for a round of Russian roulette) is, of course, stronger than the execution that came out of it. But the series is still pleasant to watch. It is a tightly organised chamber reflection on fixating on missed chances and on devaluing one’s own life. The closest comparison, it seems to me, is a collection of short stories through which this paranormal premise runs as a single plot thread, while the characters change from one story to the next.

I will single out the ending in particular: it completely cancels out all the black humour that Danila Kozlovsky’s character uses so actively and puts a genuinely bright full stop at the end of the story. At the same time it is entirely convincing and closes the most mysterious storyline, which is something of a rarity. In a word, the series will definitely help you spend an autumn evening with relish.

---

## The Paper: A High-Quality Gentle Comedy in the Spirit of the Times

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/gazeta-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-09-15 (15 September 2025)
Work: “The Paper” is a 2025 series directed by Greg Daniels.
Tags: series, comedy, sitcom, American cinema
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/gazeta-serial/

While my colleagues are hard at work at Novy sezon (“New Season”, a Russian series festival), I am entertaining myself by watching [*The Paper*](https://t.me/kino_voice/839), that very spin-off of *The Office*, only now it is not just about paper but about an honest-to-goodness newspaper.

Of course, you should not expect from this series the effect of non-stop laughter that you used to get with *The Office*! But that is not a minus at all, just a small problem of our expectations tied to the predecessor series.

*The Paper* has a great set-up, distinctive characters and cringe that is groomed just enough — half of it specific to the media world, half of it universal office stuff anyone can relate to. It is a very high-quality gentle comedy in the spirit of the times, that is, a pleasant companion for any free evening. Here is a small checklist of what to expect (it is also a list of reasons to watch *The Paper*):

- Toilet paper jokes
- An Italian villainess
- Oscar from the original *The Office*
- Great opening credits showing a newspaper being used for anything except reading
- The local Jim and Pam — and we need nothing more

## DOKer Festival 2025: What to Catch Before It Closes

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/festival-doker-2025/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-09-13 (13 September 2025)
Tags: festivals, documentary, Moscow
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/festival-doker-2025/

On 14 September, Moscow’s [DOKer International Film Festival,](https://www.midff.ru/schedule) which gathers the best documentaries from all over the world, comes to a close

Personally, I am waiting for the closing for the sake of the premiere of [*Flamingos: Life After the Meteorite*.](https://www.midff.ru/product-page/flamingos). It is a touching film about how Caribbean flamingos start families. Filming took more than 9 years, and it was worth it: look at the footage of these bright cuties, you cannot tear your eyes away. It will be shown at the Oktyabr cinema, [tickets here,](https://karofilm.ru/film/14910?date=2025-09-14) so the big-screen effect is guaranteed)

Screenings at DOKer come with discussions with the filmmakers, psychologists and film critics, which is always cool. And this year’s novelty is a programme about art, DOKer Art, created together with the Béton Centre for Visual Culture, where you can see both personal portraits of renowned creators and studies of entire cultural eras.

What else you can still catch at DOKer:

- 13 September, 19.00. [*Protokol Tukdama*](https://www.midff.ru/product-page/tukdam) («Протокол Тукдама», “The Tukdam Protocol”). On the dialogue between Buddhism and modern science.
- 14 September, 14.00. [*Norsoyan*](https://www.midff.ru/product-page/norsoyan) («Норсоян»). A confession about dreams, creative freedom and the price of high fashion.

The full schedule and details are [here](https://www.midff.ru/schedule).

**Tell me, which documentaries do you love and would recommend?**

One of my favourite impressions of the recent Pilot (the Russian series festival in Ivanovo) was the first episode of the doc *ART is Me*, about circus performers who defy gravity, politely train little sheep and do other impossible things.

Today the documentary series from KION (the Russian streaming service) got a teaser.
