## Poker for Us: A Story That Ended Purely by Karma

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/nam-poker-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-06-20 (20 June 2025); updated: 2025-12-03
Work: “Poker for Us” is a 2025 series directed by Rustam Ilyasov.
Tags: festivals, series, Russian cinema, crime
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/nam-poker-serial/

## 20 June 2025

Fun and illegal, like gambling, the project *Poker for Us* (*Nam poker*) wins you over with stylish camerawork and crisp portraits of its characters from the first frame. Respect, by the way, for the pop-up explanations of gaming terms!

Three friends decide to open a poker club right in their own home, but the illegal business draws them in. The spirit of illicit fun is infectious through the screen, and now we are already rooting for the hapless owners of the gambling den.

The cast includes Artyom Koshman, Sasha Bortich and Pyotr Skvortsov (always glad to see him). As in *Popados* (“Busted”), the consequences of stepping onto the slippery slope for young people are declared from the first frame. But here my favourite mechanism works: even knowing the outcome, it is extremely curious to find out how the heroes came to live like this.

## 6 November 2025

The very likeable series [*Poker for Us*](https://t.me/kino_voice/925) also launched with two episodes.

I fell for it back in the summer at Pilot (the Russian series festival), and the review of the first episode was [written](https://t.me/kino_voice/668) right from there. The second does not slacken the pace either. In particular, Pyotr Skvortsov’s character, mysteriously announced in the first episode, unfolds further into full-blown madness. I have not seen the actor in this role of a completely unhinged villain for a long time, and it suits him very well, so the creators of *Poker for Us* have hit the jackpot here.

The very texture of the story about two students caught in an unhealthy scheme with an illegal casino is very absorbing, because it is done briskly, in a contemporary way and not as dramatically as it could have been with such a plot. Besides, the effect of the half-open ending announced in the first frames of the series immediately makes you want to find out how they came to live like this.

## 17 November 2025

Gambling-and-series addicts, are you here?

The new episodes of [*Poker for Us*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1057) are a sort of meme feast, nothing less. I am crazy about this project simply because of the density of gags that slip through the relentless bleakness. I have put together a little checklist of things better seen once than heard about 100 times:

- a recipe for pies with rat poison, with stylish subtitles
- the funeral of a granny who planted drug stashes, in the style of flamboyantly performative absurdity
- a humane debt collector played by Ruslan Bratov (the director of the cult short *Lalay-balalay*, «Лалай-балалай», a sing-song nonsense phrase)
- a lad with a rifle in a striped sailor’s vest with the vibe of Alexei Serebryakov in Balabanov’s *Cargo 200* (attaching for comparison)

## 3 December 2025

[*Poker for Us*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1089) is over.

I am as pleased with the series as can be and will be waiting intently for news of a second season (by every parameter and every hook cast, it is essential here).

Yesterday, finishing the final episode, I became definitively convinced of the thought that nothing more plausible in terms of fatalities developing in parallel in the lives of specific people has been filmed in recent years (or I have not seen it). I do not run an underground casino, of course, but all the heroes’ ordeals from the endless cycle of problems flowing out of one another I can quite understand and share. Luckily, the story in the series ended purely by karma, so there is always hope.

Egor as played by Timofey Eletsky is the best to my taste, a very deep and, for all his deceptive exterior, touchingly sweet character. Simply a one hundred percent hit on a good man who means well and because of that sometimes does badly, and you believe it. Ruslan Bratov’s (the director of the wonderful [*Express*](https://t.me/kino_voice/52)) Javid is simply a riot too: evidently the axiom “a talented person is talented in everything” worked here. Vitya (Artyom Koshman) has a wonderful character arc with the strongest transformations, also a sheer pleasure to watch, as, incidentally, does Alexandra Bortich. In humour the screenwriters simply hit the jackpot: it is worth rewatching with a notebook and copying the jokes out into your personal collection.

In short, I can praise the series for a long time, as you can see; I hope as many people as possible appreciate it. I would not want it to end after one season without ever revealing to us the context of the video message from Koshman’s character in the first episode.

## Coeval: The 1990s Not Just as a Crime Chronicle

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/rovesnik-2024/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-06-19 (19 June 2025)
Work: “Coeval” is a 2024 film directed by Fedor Kudryavtsev.
Tags: Russian cinema, 1990s, drama
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/rovesnik-2024/

Be sure to catch [*Coeval*](https://youtu.be/5_0UbyOfzM8?si=x1g73I-hlFGPw5b6) («Ровесник») in cinemas, because it is simply a contemporary phenomenon that will definitely surprise you.

A film that combines mockumentary, screenlife and neural-network technology all at once, it is also good in substance. It is a rare reflection of the 1990s in cinema that does not look like a mere crime chronicle (although there is that too), but lets you feel the spirit of the time in a completely different way. In the course of searching for the truth about his father’s past, the protagonist goes through a personal crisis of his own, and we, the viewers, get the chance to live through with him the real story of one internet company whose founders met very different fates.

A special joy is watching how successfully deepfake has been used to de-age the older generation of characters. Look at Alexander Yatsenko: he is straight out of Balabanov’s *It Doesn’t Hurt Me*, a delight! It is great that cinema is making friends with the latest technology and becoming more varied and cooler.

Speaking of technology, by the way: the filmmakers have given the protagonist his own [account,](https://youtube.com/@rovesnik_film?si=drXFwdD9vjtWA7KO) where various excerpts from his documentary are posted. A great move and a nice opportunity to rewatch some moments (and you want to do that right after leaving the cinema)

## Something Positive: The Series’ Charm Lies in the Little Things

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/chto-to-polozhitelnoe-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-06-18 (18 June 2025)
Work: “Something Positive” is a 2025 series directed by Nika Yakovleva.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, comedy
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/chto-to-polozhitelnoe-serial/

An extremely likeable series, [*Something Positive*](https://youtu.be/hvQ4ooUA_lo?si=NNkKE3djGWBPDLUt) («Что-то положительное»), starts coming out on Monday, and on the strength of three episodes one can safely say that it is a success.

The series’ charm lies in the little things.

- First, it is extremely pleasant to see Taisya Kalinina in a comic role: after her difficult parts in [*The Highway*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/trassa-serial/) and *Odin malenky nochnoy sekret* («Один маленький ночной секрет», “One Little Night Secret”), this is a real breath of fresh air. The actors playing the other characters are also perfectly cast; you cannot take your eyes off them.

- Second, the plot convention of a fake pregnancy, which the 17-year-old heroine uses to get attention from her parents and the boy of her dreams, does not put you off. Thanks to the lie being declared up front, the theme of teenage pregnancy does not slide into the repertoire of the show *Beremenna v 16* («Беременна в 16», “Pregnant at 16”, a Russian reality show) and stays within the bounds of decency, taste and style.

- Third, the heroine’s misadventures are dotted with animated inserts featuring a white cat that personifies the girl’s conscience. Visually this really freshens up everything that happens, and it also breaks the wall between the viewer and the characters a little: a kind of ally appears on screen who also assesses what is going on and, unlike the viewers, even has the chance to influence the heroine’s decisions a little)

As a bonus, I will highlight the 20-minute episodes: with that running time the series has every chance of becoming a pleasant companion for when you want to watch a light, funny story without being pulled too far away from your other plans. So far I am getting powerful vibes of [*Mamonty*](https://t.me/kino_voice/334) («Мамонты», “Mammoths”) from *Something Positive*: the same kind of undemanding story about a small family commotion that opens everyone’s eyes to something important.

## How to Train Your Dragon: An Extremely Successful Adaptation of the Animated Original

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/kak-priruchit-drakona-2025/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-06-17 (17 June 2025)
Work: “How to Train Your Dragon” is a 2025 film directed by Dean DeBlois.
Tags: remake, fantasy, family, American cinema
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/kak-priruchit-drakona-2025/

I also took a look at [*How to Train Your Dragon*](https://youtu.be/22w7z_lT6YM?si=fdLTkX6_hps4U-q2) in its updated live-action version. Because of the combination of mighty animated dragons with people, the whole thing looks a bit like a prequel to [*House of the Dragon*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/dom-drakona-serial/), along the lines of “this is how our ancestors tamed dragons, even before we split into clans and started warring with one another”.

This adaptation of the animated original is extremely successful, not least, of course, thanks to the perfect casting for young Hiccup. He is played by Mason Thames, a 17-year-old actor whom, I think, we will see more than once, and he hits the character we know from the cartoon one hundred per cent, right down to the outline of his silhouette. The same can be said of the Viking chief, played by the utterly manly Gerard Butler. The comfort and sense of recognition while watching are, accordingly, at their maximum.

A great choice for imagining that rainy summer days are the bracing climate of the Vikings’ island.

## Lilo & Stitch: The New Version Has Not Lost a Drop of Its Charm

I greatly enjoyed the new version of [*Lilo & Stitch*](https://youtu.be/m5fMyIImwEY?si=jeI01g4BXo68UnXC), which has not lost a drop of its charm compared with the original.

The animated aliens are as convincing as ever, and the live actors are perfectly cast. Hearing that very accent of Stitch’s in the Russian dub is priceless) Incidentally, the cinema itself is gorgeous: it has recently been restored and is very spacious, bright and beautiful. ## High Season: Zavtur and Popov’s Chemistry, Broken for the Sake of Intrigue

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/vysokiy-sezon-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-06-12 (12 June 2025)
Work: “High Season” is a 2025 series directed by Stas Ivanov.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, drama, adventure
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/vysokiy-sezon-serial/

In [*High Season*](https://youtu.be/XPeC2GdJogs?si=aDrQ1LeKnX-j4IdG) there are many eye-catching things: the tropical setting, the super-cool chemistry between Zavtur and Popov (always glad to see him after *Aktrisy*, “Actresses”), a mysterious set-up with the heroine vanishing in the middle of a perfect holiday with her all-but-fiancé…

However, these merits of the exposition are quickly replaced by the chaos of events that befall the characters. In the lead couple a favourite emerges (the sensible normie Misha, played by Popov) and an object of complete incomprehension (the flighty Anya, Zavtur). It was a real pleasure to see them together: the dialogue flowed as if by itself rather than from a script, the laughter was sincere and the looks were deep. But everything was broken for the sake of the opening intrigue, and now you want to pity Misha and condemn Anya.

**⤵️** The parallel crime line about a sister’s revenge is so far developing more formulaically. There was no time to immerse yourself in the heroines’ relationship (unlike the Misha and Anya pair), and so the elder sister’s despair is less believable. I would like to hope that the series pulls the second line up to the level of the first and becomes gripping on all fronts.

## The Phoenician Scheme: Wes Anderson’s Signature Style, with Exceptions

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/finikiyskaya-skhema-2025/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-06-08 (8 June 2025)
Work: “The Phoenician Scheme” is a 2025 film directed by Wes Anderson.
Tags: arthouse, comedy
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/finikiyskaya-skhema-2025/

In Wes Anderson’s [*The Phoenician Scheme*](https://www.kinopoisk.ru/film/5460719/) the director’s signature style, which we are used to, shows through more subtly than ever, but with exceptions.

There are no screamingly contrasting or, conversely, carefully matched colours in the film’s palette, and the absurdist humour characteristic of Anderson’s characters looks unusually unobtrusive. On the other hand, the work as a whole seems to leave the impression of a summing-up. The key theme of fragile family ties, which flows from film to film with this director, is in place. But there is not even any certainty that the family is real, and blood kinship, it turns out, is not so important. The motif of the journey, masking the characters’ inner transformation, now works not towards a reset of characters but towards a wholesale rebirth. And the amount of violence on screen, unusual for Anderson, seems to bring the picture closer to a reality that is not at all distinguished by multicoloured aesthetics and symmetry.

In this I see two patterns:

**1️⃣** The protagonist, who runs his business against every rule of economics, constantly survives deadly situations yet stays alive. This is very reminiscent of the path of Wes Anderson himself, who works by his own rules of cinema and with every new work survives the inevitable “death of the author” (Roland Barthes’s concept, according to which the author of a work loses authorial power over its meaning immediately upon publication). Perhaps that is exactly why the protagonist of *The Phoenician Scheme* constantly rephrases other people’s wording in business papers, just as viewers rephrase the message the authors put into films or texts.

**2️⃣** By the end (I do not think this will be a big spoiler) the characters seem to arrive at the absence of symmetrical and colour correctness altogether: what we see in the frame resembles the reality around us as never before in Wes Anderson. This seems to underline once again the importance of inner content rather than the outer, however beautiful, shell: a very soothing thought.

Though perhaps this is my viewer’s interpretation, made thanks to the phenomenon of the “death of the author”.

---

## License to Love: A Second Chance Is, First of All, Something We Must Give Ourselves

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/muzhu-privet-2025/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-06-04 (4 June 2025)
Work: “License to Love” is a 2025 film directed by Anton Maslov.
Tags: drama, Russian cinema
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/muzhu-privet-2025/

The saying that “sometimes life gives a second chance” is incomplete, and the film [*License to Love*](https://okko.tv/movie/muzhu-privet) (*Muzhu privet*, “Say Hi to Your Husband”) illustrates this very well. A second chance is, first of all, something we must give ourselves.

The best Russian film of the 2025 Moscow International Film Festival envelops you from the first frame in warmth and hope for the best. Yulia Peresild’s heroine Katerina seems ashamed to be unhappy amid the joyful newlyweds at her job at the registry office: life around her is in full swing, and her day will come (probably) when her husband wakes from his coma (5 years on from the tragedy). In parallel, Katerina’s daughter plans to rush into marriage with a promising but unloved fiancé, and her son is even trying to court a classmate of strange (if not to say absent) moral principles. It seems they all need a second chance.

Despite the utterly tragic plot, what happens on screen does not knock you off balance or make you shed tears straight away. Apparently thanks to the lightness with which Katerina overcomes adversity: she will answer the nasty old neighbour’s remark with a joke, laughing; she will look at her son’s teenage crises with an understanding smile; at work she will wink affably at the citizens in the queue. In the course of analysing the heroine, I came to the thought that such calm is given to her by certainty: her husband is stuck in a coma, and, however terrible that is, she has got used to it. The hardest part for Katerina begins with the appearance of a real choice about what to do with her life, which had seemed settled forever.

In *License to Love* there is a fleeting but important mention of a Soviet classic, *Moscow Does Not Believe in Tears*. The two films really are related by a shared mood and the display of gentle female strength in the fight for one’s own happiness. The acting in *License to Love* is top-notch too: Peresild and Vdovichenkov exist beautifully as a pair. All together, an excellent reason to drop out of reality for a couple of hours and think about the price of happiness and the number of permissible chances on the way to it.

---

## Fedor Sheyd’s Bezmyatezhnost: Absurdity, Hopelessness and Wicked Optimism

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/bezmyatezhnost-kniga/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-06-03 (3 June 2025)
Work: “Bezmyatezhnost” is a 2025 book by Fedor Sheyd.
Tags: books, black comedy
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/bezmyatezhnost-kniga/

A bookish off-topic post

If you are looking for great summer reading with an easy style and unconventional plots, take a look at Fedor Sheyd’s [*Bezmyatezhnost*](https://books.yandex.ru/books/eun01Io3) («Безмятежность», “Serenity”). It is the most powerful short-story collection I have read lately, and I am deliberately stretching out the remaining stories so that they do not run out, I like it that much)

These short texts have absurdity, and hopelessness, and wicked optimism backed up by the blackest humour (I especially value the story about working in the editorial office of a text-based outlet: the author knows well what he is writing about). In a word, an incomparable density of text with absolute formal simplicity. Naturally, you really want to see every story adapted for the screen: both the descriptions and the dialogue are very cinematic. I hope someone in the film industry will definitely spot this.

## Pilot 2025: Impressions of the Competition Pilots

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/festival-pilot-2025/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-05-31 (31 May 2025); updated: 2025-06-25
Tags: festivals, series, Russian cinema
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/festival-pilot-2025/

## 31 May 2025

Festival news!

The series festival I love so much, [Pilot,](https://t.me/pilot_festival) held in Ivanovo, where I will be from 19 to 22 June, has announced its opening series.

It will be *Konstantinopol* («Константинополь», “Constantinople”; formerly titled [*Izgoi*, “The Outcasts”)](https://www.kinopoisk.ru/series/5895344/), the story of the White émigré Neratov (Alexander Ustyugov), who lost roughly everything in the Civil War and ended up in Constantinople. But no longer as a prominent White Guard colonel: rather as an ordinary refugee and, as we can guess, one with very few rights. It is precisely for the rights of Russian émigrés that he will fight.

For the second year running, Pilot opens with a large-scale historical drama. Last year it was the slightly frantic series [*Plevako*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/plevako-serial/) about the famous lawyer of the last pre-revolutionary years, and that is an interesting coincidence.

Perhaps the last years of the Russian Empire and the beginning of the revolution are now one of the most sought-after historical parallels that cinema reflects on. So I can hardly wait to see it!

## 11 June 2025

And [here](https://t.me/pilot_festival/539) is part of the programme of Pilot (the Russian series festival in Ivanovo), which is about to begin!

In this competition, of course, I will be especially looking forward to the screening of [*The Surgeon*](https://www.kinopoisk.ru/series/5698770/) (*Khirurg*) with Sergei Gilev in the lead and [*Ne v svoey tarelke*](https://www.kinopoisk.ru/series/7389722/) («Не в своей тарелке», “Out of Sorts”), a fantasy comedy with Yuri Stoyanov and Denis Prytkov.

## 16 June 2025

And, finally, the main [competition](https://t.me/pilot_festival/541) of the Pilot festival! Time to pick the most anticipated premieres)

Personally, I am very interested in:

- *16 let i 9 mesyatsev* («16 лет и 9 месяцев», “16 Years and 9 Months”): a teenage story starring Oleg Savostyuk, whom I am always glad to see

- *Dorogoy Villi* («Дорогой Вилли», “Dear Willy”): Sergei Makovetsky as Brezhnev, come on!

- *Breathe* (*Dyshi*): a directorial work by Anna Kuznetsova, who made [*Intermission*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/kanikuly-2023/) (*Kanikuly*), a very important and notable film of last year

- *Jack Russell* (*Zheka Rassel*): Eldar Kalimulin’s character turns into a Jack Russell terrier. I am expecting a great comedy)

- *Old School* (*Oldskul*): the project about an old-school teacher has an atmospheric [teaser,](https://youtu.be/imVyvZxeS0I?si=Q74_rd-HxAF3jV6w) which really whets the appetite

- *Popados* («Попадос», “Busted”): Makar Khlebnikov and Timofey Tribuntsev at the centre of a crime story, a promising duo (especially judging by Tribuntsev and Minekaev’s experience in [*Overheard in Rybinsk*)](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/podslushano-v-rybinske-serial/)

I will write about all of it from the festival.

## 19 June 2025

And over the next 4 days the channel will have lots of reviews of what I have watched at the Pilot festival (the Russian series festival in Ivanovo).

It is my second festival, and I had been really looking forward to the trip: it is always a celebration of cinema and a chance to talk to all kinds of people from the industry.

This time 17 “pilots” are taking part in the competition: first episodes of series that will later (most of them) come out on our streaming services. Look out for reviews (and [here](https://t.me/kino_voice/646) I have gathered descriptions of the premieres I am most looking forward to)! Last year, for example, Pilot showed [*Ona takaya klassnaya*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/ona-takaya-klassnaya-serial/) (“She’s So Cool”) and [*Give a Show!*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/dayte-shou-serial/), which later took off big time.

The festival also has an industry programme and a competition of documentary series: I will try to write about the most interesting news from there. And at the end the jury hands out awards in various categories: namely, to the best pilot, the best actor/actress and so on. Last year it was very interesting to [compare](https://t.me/kino_voice/129) my guesses with the jury’s decision, so I am already looking forward to it.

## 19 June 2025

My colleagues backed me, so I will post a joke I came up with back when the [Pilot jury](https://t.me/pilot_festival/535) was announced

Life is not the same without a Kott! (a play on the Russian saying “life is not the same without a cat”, *kot* being Russian for “cat”)

The joke is that the 2024 jury included the director Vladimir Kott, and this year’s jury includes his brother Alexander! A surname that is compulsory at the festival)

## 19 June 2025

The festival (Pilot, the Russian series festival in Ivanovo) opens with [*Konstantinopol*](https://t.me/kino_voice/622) (“Constantinople”), which, as last year, is an exemplary classical historical drama with its own advantages and shortcomings. The adventures of refugees from the Russian Empire in Constantinople in the first episode are rather of a declarative nature and, in terms of plot, fall short of the artistic elaboration of this world.

Before us is an officer who has lost his whole family and his faith in military honour, a quick-witted doctor (so far the most interesting character, played by Kirill Käro) and a “merchant” thirsting to get back the gold confiscated by the Constantinople customs officers. Tying these lines together is difficult so far, so that will be a task mostly for the most devoted fans of the genre.

## 20 June 2025

Is it hard to adapt texts for the screen?

Mikhail Kitaev talks about it at Pilot’s industry section. You can see the arguments for and against on the slide, and on the whole, of course, it is hard to disagree that these adaptations are an extremely fascinating business and at the same time a terribly difficult one. After all, every reader already has their own picture formed in their head!

I especially liked how Kinopoisk (Russia’s largest film database, media and streaming service) played on the conflicting reviews of [*Crime and Punishment*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/prestuplenie-i-nakazanie-serial/), the cornerstone of the heated debates of autumn 2024. Half of the viewers gave it extremely high ratings, and the other half gave it 1 out of 10. In the end it came out at 5.8 on Kinopoisk. The platform collected a variety of reviews and made a superb video inviting you to pick a side — it turned out to be a great image-building piece! By the way, speaking of *Crime and Punishment*, which side are you on?)

## 20 June 2025

*Full House* is a story interesting first and foremost for its experimental nature. It combines a little medical drama, a little mysticism, a little procedural, a little of Bulgakov’s *A Young Doctor’s Notebook*. Not everything is smooth, but if they polish it, as the creators said, it is potentially a good thing.

The plot about a principled medical resident in the far north looks somewhat uncomfortable, exactly enough to convey the heroine’s state in a new place where there is zero trust from colleagues and bureaucracy and drinking surgeons all around. Incidentally, Pyotr Fyodorov is rather good as the latter. It will be interesting to see how his clearly drawn conflict with the heroine, played by Maria Lisova, develops. For the sake of such a clash of experience and idealism, it is probably worth waiting for the remaining episodes.

## 20 June 2025

Remember the title *Popados* (“Busted”): it is a brisk piece of crime action with new faces and already established artists. I was looking forward to it largely because of the duo of Makar Khlebnikov and Timofey Tribuntsev, and they really are wonderful here, playing father and son.

The plot structure neatly combines flashbacks with a present in which the consequences of the teenagers’ prank have already arrived. Flirting with the criminal world turns into big problems for the heroes, and here one recalls *Na avtomate* (“On Autopilot”), a project that reflected substantively on the same themes. The pilot gave all its lines worthy set-ups at a good pace, so one really does want to wait for the continuation.

## 21 June 2025

With all my heart I wish the project *Bukhanka Chyornogo* (“Chyorny’s Loaf”, a pun on the UAZ “loaf” van) to find its platform and be filmed to the end: it is a real discovery among the independent projects.

The hysterically funny Lyokha, the protagonist, whom I privately dubbed “the plush gangster”, works as a waiter in his father’s coffee shop, hates hipsters with their almond-milk lattes and threatens them with a pistol over complaints about the dishes (on closer inspection it is just a pistol-shaped lighter). In his room a portrait of Sasha Bely (the gangster hero of *Brigada*) hangs on the mirror, and he himself is grotesquely stuck in the 1990s, when his grandfather Grisha Chyorny ran things. In search of past greatness he goes to his grandmother’s Karelian village, where the only thing left of his grandfather’s legacy is a UAZ van, that very Chyorny’s Loaf (my applause for the project’s resourceful title). An attempt to get back his grandfather’s Merc turns into problems, and from there all that remains is to wait for a whole season)

My [*Garazhniki*](https://t.me/kino_voice/137) (“Garage People”) of 2025.

## 21 June 2025

The southern-sunny and pleasantly naive series *Vinodely* (“The Winemakers”) succinctly declares a lately favourite screenwriting device: the collision of the working class with the aestheticising bohemia.

This time a winery is to be divided. A trio of proletarians from Chelyabinsk come to Gelendzhik for the inheritance of a relative who vanished from the radar 20 years ago (and has now died altogether). The local owners (and partners of the deceased relative), played by Andrey Urgant and Elena Podkaminskaya, are in shock. Podkaminskaya, by the way, plays the winery’s manager, no less beautifully than many years ago she played the manager of a French restaurant in *Kukhnya* (“The Kitchen”, the hit sitcom).

Standard comic situations are supplemented by wine snobbery and a mismatch, let us say, of gastronomic cultures, compensated by a romantic match) I hope the story opens up like a good wine.

## 21 June 2025

It is great that many projects at this Pilot are devoted precisely to women and their problems.

*Feyk* (“Fake”) is a wonderful illustration of complete defencelessness on the internet, and following on from that, of maximum vulnerability before people who do not believe you and judge you. A real horror in which the monsters hide not under the bed but in the comments.

A kind-hearted biology teacher (Anastasia Krasovskaya, who for the second festival in a row gets heavy scenes of violence) runs into brutal online stalking: everything looks as if she is taking part in erotic correspondence under her own name. Her identity has literally been stolen. The young woman tries to find the culprit, and this gives the proceedings a swift pace and the right nerve. It is frightening and intriguing how this story might end ⬅️

## 22 June 2025

The results of the Pilot 2025 competitions are about to be announced, but my colleagues and I gathered our opinions a little earlier [in a special table by Komendant kinokreposti](https://t.me/textortexel/5837) («Комендант кинокрепости», “The Commandant of the Film Fortress”, a Telegram channel).

I am very grateful for this opportunity to exchange opinions with colleagues and get an objective assessment of what we have seen. And, of course, I will be waiting to see whether our picks coincide with the jury’s decisions.

## 22 June 2025

By the way, regarding the [vote](https://t.me/textortexel/5830) my colleagues and I held on Pilot’s main competition programme, I have a small visualisation and a few interesting facts about us!

It turns out that among us there is the kindest critic (yours truly), the strictest critic ([@ershovfilm](https://t.me/ershovfilm)) and several people whose opinions are very close to one another)

And opinions diverged most of all on the series [*Full House*](https://t.me/kino_voice/666): its spread of scores is the most noticeable! How cool that we have such different views and opinions, which we brought together and recorded.

## 25 June 2025

And the last, but not the least, in the wake of Pilot!

Kinopoisk (Russia’s largest film database, media and streaming service) and I gathered all the series of the showcase into one [piece](https://www.kinopoisk.ru/media/article/4011387/), for which I wrote about 9 of the 18 series. I highly recommend it as a retrospective and as a watchlist for the future) *(by the way, as an extra bit of entertainment while reading, you can try to guess from the writing style exactly which of the series* I covered *myself)*

And I also had a small hand in the [piece](https://www.kinopoisk.ru/media/news/4011391/) about the industry programme: it gave us not only the much-discussed [portrait](https://t.me/kino_voice/671) of the average Russian woman, but also some interesting news and anticipated projects. Short and to the point!

## Fisher. Zatmenie: Greatness in Its Purest Form

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/fisher-zatmenie-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-05-29 (29 May 2025); updated: 2025-12-12
Work: “Fisher. Zatmenie” is a 2025 series directed by Alexander Tsoi.
Tags: series, mystery, Russian cinema
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/fisher-zatmenie-serial/

## 29 May 2025

[*Fisher. Zatmenie*](https://youtu.be/_7QB_MyZ1gI?si=t-jsRQLNmEpuN-Up) («Фишер. Затмение», “Fisher. Eclipse”, the second season of the hit crime series) pleases from the first episode: Bokov is in excellent form, Yatsenko in his role wisecracks like a god, and Starshenbaum’s heroine looks right at home in this company.

The first frames, where Bokov interrogates Fisher in prison, are as if straight out of the world of [*Autsors*,](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/autsors-serial/) (“Outsource”) and evoke a pleasant feeling of recognition (if that is intentional, cool). The exposition works like clockwork: there is a tail end of the old case, an extended (despite the episode’s running time of only 40 minutes!) introduction of new characters, and a humanising of the characteristic traits of the old ones.

Bokov, who kept saying “Sho?” (“What?”) in season 1, for instance, has acquired a little dog, naturally named Sho. I hope the doggie does not come to harm in the course of catching the maniac.

## 5 June 2025

A checklist for fighting stress according to the second episode of [*Fisher. Zatmenie*](https://t.me/kino_voice/619)

- Learn a foreign language so you can switch to it in the worst moments and catch derealisation. If you are lucky, also rhyme it with Russian swearing, like Bokov.

- Set up a fight club with deviant elements in a rough neighbourhood. Be reborn spiritually and physically.

- Terrorise the star of the local radio station and make a coded announcement for criminals so that the whole town keeps calling in, trying to collect a bag of money. Watch.

Whether these methods work, we will find out in the next episodes.

## 20 June 2025

Even in festival conditions I could not miss the new episode of [*Fisher*](https://t.me/kino_voice/631): the midpoint of the season whets the appetite for the resolution to the maximum.

Besides the magnificently worked-out plot (to my taste, more powerful than in the first season!), the series’ speech specifics are gaining momentum too. This is the most linguistically distinctive series of recent times. Outdone, perhaps, only by [*El Ruso*,](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/el-ruso-serial/) where the actors talked like Old Believers)

But the virtuoso use of profanity by Yankovsky’s and Starshenbaum’s characters makes you want to literally write it down and quote it. Whichever way you look at it, such speech adds a hefty dose of sincerity and realism to everything that happens, which is extremely important for this crime story.

## 26 June 2025

[*Fisher*](https://t.me/kino_voice/659) is not only breaking records on the [Kinopoisk Pro Index](https://t.me/kinopoisk_Industry/5427) but also sharply (and, like Bokov, boldly) turning off the planned plot trajectory.

Having “slipped”, as Bokov put it (I never stop admiring him) at the very end of the fresh episode, the investigation is forced to change direction sharply? One would like to hope that the outcome of the investigation will not boil down to the formula “the butler did it” and that the criminal will not be as close at hand as he now seems.

And this episode has more of Yatsenko’s character and of Fisher himself. Andrey Maksimov is an amazing actor, of course: before watching the pilot episode of [*Normalny*](https://t.me/kino_voice/679) (“Normal”), where he plays a man on the autism spectrum, I could not imagine him in the role of even a remotely positive character (not a gangster and not a maniac). And now, what do you think? I cannot perceive him in *Fisher* as a maniac: he is such a sweet, kind guy. But all this, of course, is a joke; this is how I praise stunning transformations and a 180-degree change of type.

## 5 July 2025

Meanwhile the second season of [*Fisher*](https://t.me/kino_voice/706) has decided after all to be more cruel than the first and to take my favourite character away from me.

In the sixth episode everything twists mightily around one particular character whom I had come to love over the season, and it seems it will not end well. On the other hand, over the next two episodes I will definitely have time to enjoy how well the screenwriters have brought together a heap of storylines that at first seemed disparate. Sectarians, a nasty official, local gangsters: all this turns out to be intertwined and involved in the approaching resolution.

Also, incidentally, Andrey Maksimov seems to have been lucky this season to play every facet of Fisher, and it looks very, very convincing. And most importantly, the line with his interrogations does not seem at all extraneous or foreign to what is going on in Kurortny; on the contrary, it seems to let us look retrospectively at the search for the new maniac and build our own guesses based on their (the maniacs’) logic.

## 17 July 2025

In my opinion, the finale of the series [*Fisher. Zatmenie*](https://t.me/kino_voice/619) is greatness in its purest form. Besides all manner of praise for the work itself, I will follow with great interest the future roles of Nikita Khudyakov, who played Vanya Zlobin, because in this story he showed himself to be a very powerful artist. Watching him was a real pleasure.

The resolution looks quick, rhythmic and without unnecessary preludes, but with an elegant sprinkling of devilry ➡️ For me this is the perfect outcome: I do not like detective stories where the intrigue drags on and on, forcing us to watch the investigators’ train of thought for an indecently long time; personally I find it easy to drop such viewing. To the last I wished that this would not happen with *Fisher*, and my wishes came true. I had [guesses,](https://t.me/kino_voice/725) but in reality everything is done more cunningly, literally as unpredictable as fate itself, and that, it seems, is the height of craftsmanship. I liked the detail of Zlobin’s transfer “from somewhere up north”: *Fisher* has more in common with *Autsors* than it seems.

Separately, I cannot help admiring the character posters: bamboo, a mourning ribbon, bees; a good set of details both for those who have not yet watched and for those who already know everything.

Naturally, my book of quotations did not go without additions from Bokov’s lexicon. The line about how “I don’t need to say it twice” I will remember for a long time. May this feature continue in the future, if *Fisher* becomes an anthology with an immortal Bokov from season to season.

## 18 July 2025

The more I think about the [resolution](https://t.me/kino_voice/762) of the second *Fisher*, the more additional meanings I find.

First, I read an [interview](https://seance.ru/articles/fisher-zatmenie) with the screenwriters, Sergei Kalvarsky and Natalya Kapustina. It turns out we owe the atmosphere of the series to *Assa*. ~~Those who know me are aware:~~ It is my most beloved film, but not once while watching did I catch myself making the association, and now it has hiiit me. That is what explains this convincing counterpoint that makes you suspect rot even in the sweetest character.

On the other hand, I have plenty of cultural associations regarding Zlobin, who split into twins, and that is my second point. In the few seconds they were shown on screen together, I managed to recall both Cronenberg and Balabanov. The former because of the film *Dead Ringers*, about twins who villainously swapped places at work and in life (literally, even with women). And from Balabanov, the screenplay *My Brother Died*, with its telling title and a truly Balabanovian plot. And most importantly, a resolution that quite mirrors that of *Fisher*.

## 2 August 2025

To round off the conversation about *Fisher. Zatmenie*, I went through [the most common questions](https://www.kinopoisk.ru/media/article/4011553/): who vanished where, who came from where, and who survived?

My favourite thought is the one about Zlobin’s wardrobe; it came to me while I was writing, entirely unplanned. Zlobin’s wardrobe consists mostly of turtlenecks that cover the throat, with a scarf on top as well, so that nobody could possibly make out anything there. And at the end, as we know, Zlobin turned up with his throat cut, as part of the cunning twin plan. Obviously not for the first time, and it is precisely the consequences of previous “plans” that are hidden behind the cosy necks of his sweaters.

## 12 December 2025

Shock content: the “bad” Zlobin from [*Fisher*](https://t.me/kino_voice/762) is not the one we think

A month ago I was on the set of a [podcast](https://vk.com/video-195528184_456244235) by Wink (the Russian streaming service) about the series *Fisher. Zatmenie*, as the podcast’s scriptwriter (thanks to my colleagues for the invitation and the trust). For a scriptwriter, by the time of shooting the main work has already been done: what remains is to watch the text come to life and enjoy the blissful atmosphere, which is what I did. Now, by the way, I understand why screenwriter Alim Beschokov [on the set of *Ira*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/ira-2-sezon-intervyu-olerinskaya/) looked so happy))

As you know, I am the biggest fan of the second season, and especially of its finale. All the more joyful it was for me to listen to the discussion between Nikita Khudyakov and director Alexander Tsoi (who, by the way, is much more cheerful in life than the films he works on).

Two points you will not learn anywhere else:

**1️⃣** Of the two Zlobin twins, all the most terrible deeds were committed by Vanya, the one who was in plain sight and sobbed over the child’s death! We learned this from Nikita during a break and immediately asked him to say it on the record: nobody would have believed it had the actor not said it himself.

**2️⃣** The recipe has been revealed for the mixture that the actors, excuse me, throw up on camera. The ingredients are raw eggs, oatmeal and sugar. Ordinary groceries, but this, as they say, is one not to try at home.

The rest is in the [podcast](https://vk.com/video-195528184_456244235)) If *Fisher* is your thing, do not miss it.

---

## Other People’s Money: Dashing Crypto Crime with Two Maxim Matveevs

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/chuzhie-dengi-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-05-28 (28 May 2025); updated: 2025-06-07
Work: “Other People’s Money” is a 2025 series directed by Igor Tverdokhlebov.
Tags: series, crime, Russian cinema
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/chuzhie-dengi-serial/

## 28 May 2025

A little later, I started [*Other People’s Money*](https://youtu.be/4JuxiHkwp64?si=wXLxHfRx4WL8dGcD) (*Chuzhie dengi*), a dashing piece of crypto crime with two Maxim Matveevs (hello to *Amur*, *Mickey 17*, *Vasily* and other [films with twins).](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/bliznetsy-v-rossiyskikh-proektakh/)

The first thing that impresses pleasantly is the camerawork. The camera flies, zooms in on the characters’ faces and on objects, dollies in and out to the rhythm of the showdowns between characters, and even films them from a hidden-camera angle. Such visual variety literally rivets the gaze: it has been a long time since I was drawn into a series precisely by the cinematography. This is a rare phenomenon among contemporary projects and therefore a winning decision.

Watching Matveev in two guises is also extremely interesting; it is especially pleasing that the long-playing one turned out to be not the self-assured personality but the modest version of the hero, capable of character transformation. Despite a plot that is absolutely fantastical in current realities, the very idea of making something about good old swindlers operating with the latest technology and bitcoin is really rather appealing. In short, every factor speaks for continuing to watch.

## 7 June 2025

It is great that [*Other People’s Money*](https://t.me/kino_voice/617) not only kept its camerawork trick right up to the finale but did not let us down in the script either.

Events unfolded in such a way that the finale brings a great deal of moral satisfaction. Behind the numerous cunning schemes with crypto and cash-outs, viewers had to choose their favourite ~~Twix bar~~ version of Maxim Matveev, and the authors did the same for an effective resolution. An understandable attitude of hatred mixed with pity arose towards Svin (“Pig”), and, though Gosha Kutsenko’s character is utterly distinctive, you do not sympathise with him that much. Alina (Stasya Miloslavskaya), of course, is not without questions, but did nothing radically bad (and, accordingly, did not deserve it).

It is as if the series, which resembles science fiction more than reality, ended fantastically fairly. And that, of course, is a pleasant rarity for the empathetic viewer.

## EuroTrip: A Film You Want to Rewatch Right After the Last Shot

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/evrotur-2004/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-05-27 (27 May 2025)
Work: “EuroTrip” is a 2004 film directed by Jeff Schaffer.
Tags: comedy, American cinema, road movie, 2000s
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/evrotur-2004/

Continuing my reviews of [not new but very cool projects,](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/yuzzz-serial/) I want to tell you about *EuroTrip*, a film which, even if you have not seen it, you definitely know from its meme moments (here is my favourite, instead of a trailer)

Imagine a mix of *Piter FM* (the 2006 St Petersburg rom-com) and *What We Do in the Shadows* (only without the vampires, and with a strong friendship full of comic situations and jokes about Eastern Europe), and you get something roughly close in romance and comedy. *EuroTrip* has the stunning aura of a summer trip that you remember for the rest of your life, and at the same time unformulaic humour, so do not lump it together with *American Pie* or *Superbad*: it is a different thing) And the most interesting thing is that it is the kind of film you want to rewatch right after the last shot, and that is not such a frequent phenomenon. You especially find yourself gazing at the architecture and exteriors the characters find themselves in, despite the fact that in reality 95% of *EuroTrip* was shot in Prague, and sights like Big Ben were added to the frame by compositing.

And as always, share in the comments: which missed classics have you been catching up on lately?

## Radio Day: A Live Look at What We Are Used to Seeing as a Film

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/den-radio-teatr/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-05-26 (26 May 2025)
Work: “Radio Day” is a 2001 stage production directed by Sergey Petreykov.
Tags: theatre, comedy
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/den-radio-teatr/

Another theatrical off-topic post. This time about a production that I had rewatched as a film some 8 times.

It is *Den radio* («День радио», “Radio Day”), a show that Kvartet I (the Moscow comedy troupe) have been performing for 25 years now and that has existed as a [film](https://www.kinopoisk.ru/film/402979/) since 2008. The production is good precisely as a live look at what we are used to seeing in the fixed format of film. On stage the intonations are livelier and the characters more three-dimensional; I was especially impressed by Nonna Grishaeva, who seems not to have changed at all over these 25 years) By the way, every signature “*maladtsy!*” (“well done!”; put a ❤️ if you read it in that very intonation)) from Leonid Barats’s character is met with applause by the audience, and it is great to see that with your own eyes. But make sure you do not know all the jokes from the film literally by heart before you go, otherwise the wow effect is somewhat dulled

Why go to the theatre, you will ask, when there is both the film and a [television version of the play?](https://hd.kinopoisk.ru/film/45a12e6a541b9258be4d0bbd8613dae9) One nuance: in neither of these versions will you see the magnificent Pavel Maykov performing songs as the frontmen of several bands. Every musical number is an explosion of energy, comedy and artistry from Maykov and the band Bobry. It was this artist’s participation in the production that was the deciding factor for me: Maykov does not have many theatre roles, and watching him perform is always a great pleasure.

## Couple vs. Couple: A Comedy with a Straight Face and Slightly Philosophical Humour

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/para-na-paru-2025/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-05-22 (22 May 2025)
Work: “Couple vs. Couple” is a 2025 film directed by Vladimir Kott.
Tags: comedy, Russian cinema
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/para-na-paru-2025/

In cinemas from today: [*Couple vs. Couple*](https://t.me/kino_voice/595) (*Para na paru*), a comedy with a straight face and slightly philosophical humour

The film turned out deeper and more many-layered than the promotional materials suggest, with their promise of the familiar format of a comedy about a deceived husband and his little trick for love’s sake. In fact we get a hilarious story about the tragedy of Kostya, a desperate literature teacher; this little and at the same time superfluous man is brilliantly played by Dmitry Chebotarev. For the sake of meeting his wife, who is ignoring him hard and has already moved in with a new rich suitor (the comic Alexander Robak), Chebotarev’s hero makes a pass at his student, the daughter of that very suitor, and goes to meet “his girlfriend’s” father at their family estate (given its scale, there is no other word for it).

From there begins the heroes’ long journey towards one another and towards themselves, but the main thing is how it is done! Arguing with a family of connoisseurs of everything material, to whose side his wife has also gone over, Kostya tries to prove the value of the spiritual, the importance of art and feelings, not only of calculation. He endlessly quotes poetry (in Chebotarev’s delivery you could just listen and listen), performs small feats and makes big sacrifices. But at first he beats against it like peas against a wall, against the impenetrable loyalty to everything carnal and physical on the part of the rich masters not only of this huge house but, as it seems at first glance, of life as a whole.

As Vladimir Kott, the director of *Couple vs. Couple*, said at the premiere, a film always turns out a little different from what was originally intended. And I want to add that it is precisely for the sake of this surprise that the film is worth seeing in a cinema (your mood, like the director’s, will definitely lift).

---

## Red Rocket: The Story of a Textbook “Superfluous Man”

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/krasnaya-raketa-2021/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-05-20 (20 May 2025)
Work: “Red Rocket” is a 2021 film directed by Sean Baker.
Tags: drama, American cinema
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/krasnaya-raketa-2021/

On Saturday I went to a cycling festival and rode the whole Garden Ring (Moscow’s inner ring road), and that same evening I watched a film whose protagonist also gets around mainly by bike. Coincidence? I don’t think so

I had kept [*Red Rocket*](https://youtu.be/P0nnJljdryw?si=aBZGEzWPAeW7ih95) in mind for a long time: I liked [*Anora*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/anora-2024/) so much that I wanted to get to know something else from Sean Baker’s filmography. My high expectations were fully justified: the picture turned out to be an impressive, many-layered story of an antihero towards whom you feel completely opposite emotions for all 2 hours. Thanks to the clear division of the stages of the moral fall of Mikey, the protagonist, the film becomes a truly unique emotional attraction that the viewer, willy-nilly, lives through.

By and large, what we have is the story of a textbook “superfluous man” (the classic figure of Russian literature) trying with all his might to make himself. And the main thing Sean Baker emphasises among the reasons for his failure is the closedness of a society bound by norms and unwilling to socialise a former porn actor. It is precisely the silent refusal of any socially approved work that pushes Mikey onto the slippery path we watch for the next 2 hours. And on that slippery path (yes, yes, the one Mikey travels on his bicycle) acquiring the prefix “anti-” to the title “hero” could not be easier. The question of whether the winner takes it all, as the song “The Winner Takes It All” goes, hangs as an ominous pause in the finale. (And, it seems, the answer to it can partly be guessed already in the director’s next film, *Anora*, which continues the same theme of social outcasts).

By the way, do not watch on an empty stomach, buy some doughnuts: you are guaranteed to want them)

---

## There: The Journey Sometimes Matters More Than the Final Destination

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/tuda-2025/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-05-15 (15 May 2025)
Work: “There” is a 2025 film directed by Ivan Petukhov.
Tags: Russian cinema, road movie, dramedy
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/tuda-2025/

About the road movie [*There* (*Tuda*),](https://youtu.be/x_oLucseql4?si=D4ko8gtsdB9j59Ml) which opens in cinemas today, I had seen all sorts of opinions, so I was a little apprehensive before watching, but needlessly. You could say it turned out to be [*Kentavr*](https://www.kinopoisk.ru/film/5235968/) («Кентавр», “The Centaur”), but with good vibes)

The film about a taxi ride to Ufa and back is deftly built in terms of the script. Watching the endless dialogue between Irina Starshenbaum’s chatty heroine and the sullen driver played by Pyotr Fyodorov was pleasant and intriguing, and the main thing is that it is done convincingly enough. It is precisely the dialogue that is the best thing in this film, and the actors have mastered it 100% (this goes for the cameo characters of Serebryakov and Dobrovolskaya too, by the way).

Despite a weakish finale (a meeting with the classmates who hurt the main heroine many years ago), the film reminds us that the journey sometimes matters more than the final destination. The same can be said about the friendship that springs up between the scatterbrained passenger and the driver, and about the experience of watching this film.

## Alexandr Khant to Direct Fury: High Hopes After Mezhsezonye

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/aleksandr-khant-furiya/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-05-14 (14 May 2025)
Work: “Fury” is a work  Alexandr Khant.
Tags: Russian cinema, series, comics, announcements
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/aleksandr-khant-furiya/

Since Monday I have been rejoicing at the news that Alexandr Khant will direct the adaptation of the comic about Fury from Bubble (the Russian comics publisher) and Kinopoisk (Russia’s largest film database, media and streaming service). To explain my joy, I will tell you why my hopes are so high.

Khant’s [*Mezhsezonye*](https://youtu.be/_B5tn0EXFAU?si=UmXln91Wi-X3N9xp) («Межсезонье», “Off Season”) I still [consider](https://t.me/kino_voice/542) one of the best of all the films I have seen. This story pays enormous attention precisely to its female characters: their emotionality, their sense of the world, their self-determination. Young Sasha, the film’s protagonist, is crafted with such attention and care in every respect that there is no doubt whatsoever about the director’s skill in handling young heroines ready to challenge this world.

The comic adaptation also promises to show an alternative Moscow. There should be no problems with that either, as the example of *Mezhsezonye* shows us: you only have to recall how three-dimensional and alive Yekaterinburg appeared in Khant’s film, how the city spoke with the characters and with the viewers. Visual language is the director’s strong suit, and in the case of a comic adaptation that is no small factor)

We are waiting for *Fury* («Фурия») in 2026 (and meanwhile rewatching *Mezhsezonye* and, I hope, catching [*Dzhekpot*](https://t.me/kino_voice/112) (“Jackpot”) in cinemas)

---

## Vermiglio: It Is Not About the Village but About the Women Who Live in It

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/gornaya-nevesta-2024/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-05-13 (13 May 2025)
Work: “Vermiglio” is a 2024 film directed by Maura Delpero.
Tags: drama, European cinema
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/gornaya-nevesta-2024/

The synopsis of [*Vermiglio*](https://www.kinopoisk.ru/film/6038922/) (released in Russia as *Gornaya nevesta*, “The Mountain Bride”; it recently came out on streaming services) puts the emphasis on how a soldier who has fled the war changes the life of a mountain village in Italy. In my opinion, that is not quite right.

As you watch, it becomes clear that it is not about the village but about the women who live in it. Against the background of the decline of the patriarchal family with a man at its head (exactly the kind of family we see throughout the film), the relationships of a mother and her daughters, and of friends and sisters among themselves, come to the fore. The soldier who suddenly appears and disappears serves as a catalyst of character development only for the heroines (all the male characters, it seems, stay as they were). This dramatic circumstance, imperceptible at first glance, sets the film apart favourably from other stories about the home front of the Second World War and makes its concerns unconventional.

Incidentally, another highlight of *Vermiglio* is its visual look. The cinematography is by Mikhail Krichman, Andrey Zvyagintsev’s* regular cinematographer and the author of signature cold, detached shots, whether of nature or of characters in close-up. It is pleasing that, despite the chosen style, the finale of *Vermiglio* is nothing like the unambiguous resolutions of *Leviathan* or *Loveless*, which means a fresh cinematic impression is guaranteed.

* Andrey Zvyagintsev (Звягинцев Андрей Петрович) has been designated a “foreign agent” by Russia’s Ministry of Justice (listed on 18 September 2026).

---

## The Postman: A White Lie, a Convincing Petrov and a Questionable Ending

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/pochtar-2025/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-05-08 (8 May 2025)
Work: “The Postman” is a 2025 film directed by Andrey Razenkov.
Tags: Russian cinema, war film, drama
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/pochtar-2025/

Out of curiosity about the plot I watched [*The Postman*](https://kion.ru/video/movie/1225683588) (*Pochtar*) with Alexander Petrov and had a rather ambiguous viewing experience.

Petrov’s character, a village postman who is a bit of a holy fool, at the time of the Great Patriotic War (the Second World War), has been delivering letters all his life and knows every resident by sight. But when death notices start arriving from the front, the postman cannot find the strength to hand them to the women, so for the common good he decides to write letters on behalf of the fallen and deliver them to those who are, in essence, already widows.

I was curious how such a set-up would unfold: how will this white lie end up? Unfortunately, the ending (towards which strange musings on the benefits and harms of truth also crop up) feels contrived and not very realistic. But despite all the questionable points, what truly graces the film is, first, Petrov’s acting — he is very convincing in this complex role — and, second, the absence of the bombast typical of war films of recent years. If you like quiet cinema that makes you reflect on commonly accepted moral norms, then *The Postman* will be just the thing.

---

## Death of a Unicorn: An Epic Comedy of the Absurd with a Critique of the Present

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/smert-edinoroga-2025/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-05-06 (6 May 2025)
Work: “Death of a Unicorn” is a 2025 film directed by Alex Scharfman.
Tags: horror, comedy
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/smert-edinoroga-2025/

Yesterday [*Death of a Unicorn*](https://okko.tv/movie/death-of-a-unicorn) appeared on streaming services: an epic comedy of the absurd with a critique of the present and horror moments.

Despite a stock, sketch-like set-up (a careerist father at odds with his enlightened daughter, though both have been traumatised by a shared loss), the film grows stronger both in script and in ideas with the appearance of the unicorn itself. Besides the horror component familiar from other hits of the A24 studio, *Death of a Unicorn* stands out for the irony in whose atmosphere everything happens. Yes, there are the usual concerns of late capitalism, social inequality and ecological catastrophe, but with a smirk that takes the humour to blackness and complete absurdity. To my taste, such moves let you avoid taking the film too seriously, and therefore think over the problems shown in a calmer format.

Incidentally, the new release is in many ways reminiscent of [*Mickey 17*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/mikki-17-2025/) in its madcap image of the powers that be and other details. In *Death of a Unicorn* at some point it even comes to choosing a kind of “expendables” (exactly [the role](https://t.me/kino_voice/388) Pattinson played in *Mickey 17*). So it turns out to be an unexpected recommendation not only for fans of contemporary horror and social themes but also for lovers of Korean cinema with black humour and a dystopian mood.

## Summer Will Come: A Frightening Black-and-White Dream with an Unpredictable Ending

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/nastupit-leto-2024/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-05-03 (3 May 2025)
Work: “Summer Will Come” is a 2024 film directed by Kirill Sultanov.
Tags: Russian cinema, drama, arthouse
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/nastupit-leto-2024/

[*Summer Will Come*](https://hd.kinopoisk.ru/film/0d4997e6e35d4e79913a380659905ac8) (*Nastupit leto*) is one of those films that leave more questions than answers after you watch them.

To me the picture is like a frightening black-and-white dream, disturbing above all because its ending is impossible to predict. This effect arises because none of the characters is fully in control of their life: they all seem to drift along an uncontrollable current of external factors with no way of changing their trajectory. And this detachment from reality is also emphasised by the black-and-white cinematography, which you rarely see in modern cinema.

Incidentally, despite the powerful crime intrigue announced in the trailer, in reality the plot is not that twisty. Mark Eydelshteyn’s character certainly draws attention to himself, but looks more like a carefully thought-out script construct (a childhood trauma, the misanthropic make-up of a psychopath) than a rounded character. On the other hand, real empathy is born from watching the couple played by Mikita Voronov and Tina Stoyilkovich: the way their relationship is reflected on screen has a shot-for-shot quotation of *July Rain* (Marlen Khutsiev’s 1966 film), and sincerity, and cinematic flair.

All in all, the film leaves mixed impressions, but it definitely hooks you with its unconventional visual language, which stands out against the general background.

## Unprincipled in St-Petersburg: The Spin-Off That Let Kristina Babushkina Truly Shine

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/besprintsipnye-v-pitere-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-05-02 (2 May 2025)
Work: “Unprincipled in St-Petersburg” is a 2025 series directed by Zaur Zaseev.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, comedy
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/besprintsipnye-v-pitere-serial/

[*Unprincipled in St-Petersburg*](https://www.kinopoisk.ru/series/5377368/) (*Besprintsipnye v Pitere*) timed it nicely by catching the frosty weather of the May holidays, when even just watching a sunny city on screen is already a pleasure.

By the way, the sequel being set in exactly this location was no surprise to me: the characters, as Alexander Tsypkin [told](https://music.yandex.ru/album/14629532/track/113555328?utm_source=web&amp;utm_medium=copy_link) me on a podcast back in 2023[,](https://music.yandex.ru/album/14629532/track/113555328) would definitely go to St Petersburg one day. What was unexpected is that my favourite couple, Aglaya Tarasova and Pavel Tabakov, dropped out of the cast. Other viewers will surely miss their favourite characters too, because many of them are gone)

But every cloud has a silver lining: the spin-off lets Valya, played by Kristina Babushkina, open up superbly and show every shade of her character. Igor Vernik is interesting to watch as a theatre critic who keeps the whole cultural capital (as St Petersburg is called) in fear no worse than the mafia does. This touch of the fantastic even freshens up the familiar humour of the unprincipled crew. It is also nice to see Anna Kovalchuk: she fitted into this world perfectly from the very first frame and made a great addition to the female cast.

## Legends from the Past: Costumes as the Film’s Calling Card

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/legendy-nashikh-predkov-2025/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-04-29 (29 April 2025); updated: 2025-07-11
Work: “Legends from the Past” is a 2025 film directed by Ivan Sosnin.
Tags: Russian cinema, fairy tales
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/legendy-nashikh-predkov-2025/

## 29 April 2025

I am [continuing](https://t.me/kino_voice/538) to tell you about the charms of the film [*Legends from the Past*,](https://youtu.be/uI3T9AGLjOc?si=kAcpej7S-i9jobt4) (*Legendy nashikh predkov*), and the first thing I want to draw attention to, without spoilers for now, is the costumes! It is they, I think, that can be considered one of the film’s calling cards.

I was sincerely impressed by how elaborately the fairy-tale creatures’ appearance is worked out, in particular the shaggy forest Nyulesmurt (Anton Kuznetsov) and the water spirit Shishiga (Natalya Pavlenkova). Given current film trends, they could have drawn in all the complex details of the costumes with graphics and left it at that. But here, and it shows in the photos from the set, every hair on Nyulesmurt is real and three-dimensional (look how in the first photo they are combing his back and at the same time putting on a clawed glove), and every gill and fin on Shishiga is textured and in relief (again, there is even a close-up photo). So the combined effect of the acting and the characters’ appearance is absolutely stunning.

It all looks like a cool continuation of the tradition of the Soviet fairy-tale costume: compare Georgy Millyar in his roles in *Varvara-krasa, dlinnaya kosa* (“Barbara the Fair with the Silken Hair”) and *Morozko* (“Jack Frost”). That Baba Yaga, I think, many people remembered as the model one for life, and again, no graphics: everything rests on the imagination of the costume designers and the actor’s charisma. So *Legends from the Past*, which has all this, is worth seeing)

## 1 May 2025

In cinemas at last from today: [*Legends from the Past*](https://t.me/kino_voice/559), in my view the best contemporary film fairy tale, which has:

- Alexander Yatsenko as a journalist, a father, a keeper of legends and simply a charming bungler
- Characters from folklore unfamiliar to us, that of Udmurtia and Khanty-Mansiysk
- The song “Mesto dlya shaga vperyod” (“Room for a Step Forward”) by the band [Kino](https://zvuk.com/track/55138259) on the soundtrack
- Springtime-beautiful natural locations (and the scenes in town, incidentally, include a lot of writing on the walls of buildings, fences and other elements of the landscape: the town seems to talk to the characters and to us)
- An atmosphere of magic and hope (as in many other films by Ivan Sosnin)

I wrote a little more about this picture [in a piece for Kinopoisk](https://www.kinopoisk.ru/media/news/4011107/), and I declare with full responsibility that it is a must-have of film leisure this weekend.

## 11 July 2025

As the number one fan of [*Legends from the Past*,](https://t.me/kino_voice/569) I wrote about the film for Kinopoisk in a [list](https://www.kinopoisk.ru/media/article/4011434/) of the best Russian films of the half-year.

It seems it really is my favourite of the past half of 2025, because in my personal ranking it was not overtaken by [*The Poet*,](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/prorok-2025/) or [*Mickey 17*,](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/mikki-17-2025/) or even the wonderful [*The Phoenician Scheme*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/finikiyskaya-skhema-2025/).

Watch *Legends* on the [platforms,](https://okko.tv/movie/legendy-nashikh-predkov) if you have not yet, and share my feelings.

## From the Life of the ***ed Up: A Set of Sketches on the Absurdity of Social Norms

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/iz-zhizni-nutykh-teatr/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-04-26 (26 April 2025)
Work: “Iz zhizni ***nutykh” is a 2016 stage production directed by Yury Muravitsky.
Tags: theatre
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/iz-zhizni-nutykh-teatr/

Another theatrical off-topic post. While waiting for Alexander Khant’s [*Dzhekpot*](https://www.kinopoisk.ru/film/5266958/?utm_referrer=www.google.com) (“Jackpot”), I decided to go to a production in which he plays one of the leads. The production is called [*Iz zhizni \*\*\*nutykh*,](https://teatrdoc.ru/performances/1253/?afisha_open_widget=1) (“From the Life of the \*\*\*ed Up”), it runs at [Teatr.doc](https://t.me/Theatredoc) (the Moscow documentary theatre) and lives up to its name quite well)

Over an hour or so the viewer gets to see a set of sketches from different moments in the lives of random people: they can take place in a notional café, office, bedroom or station. As a mechanism it roughly resembles *6 kadrov* (“6 Frames”, the Russian sketch-comedy show) or flicking through Reels, only at a slower tempo, in an atmosphere of strict minimalism, light absurdism and an emotionlessness unusual for theatre (which causes no small discomfort)

The thread running through the production is the thought of the absurdity of social norms. It is not done to show concern for strangers, to talk to people you do not know, still less to show intolerance towards someone who annoys you in a public place. In the production the characters (they are the \*\*\*ed up) follow precisely the opposite rules: they poke their noses into other people’s business, try to strike up conversations with strangers and even kick street musicians whose false notes are impossible to listen to. How to interpret what you see is an individual task, but it is definitely impossible to leave the production indifferent.

---

## Stills from Favourite Films in the Ghibli Style: A Neural Network Experiment

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/kadry-v-stile-ghibli/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2025-04-26 (26 April 2025)
Tags: notes, pop culture
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/kadry-v-stile-ghibli/

At last I have got round to restyling stills from my favourite films in the Ghibli animation style, starting with the classics (Pchyola, of *Brigada*, the cult 2002 Russian gangster series, is, as always, the most handsome).

It is nice that you can now experiment with a neural network without leaving Telegram, in the bot [@gpt4telegrambot](https://t.me/gpt4telegrambot). It is simple there:
- you press the command [/wow](https://t.me/GPT4Telegrambot?start),
- attach a photo of the character
- describe your task (for example, which style to redraw the still in).
Voilà!

By the way, through the [bot](https://t.me/GPT4Telegrambot) you can also make those very figurines of characters in little boxes, your own Telegram stickers and even humanisations of animals: you can see what kind of person your cat or dog would be (I am leaving what came out with my cat in the comments).
